### <a id="terminology"></a>2&#46;1 Terminology[](#terminology)

This specification refers to both HTML and XML attributes and IDL attributes&#44; often in the same context&#46; When it is not clear which is being referred to&#44; they are referred to as <strong>content attributes</strong> for HTML and XML attributes&#44; and <strong>IDL attributes</strong> for those defined on IDL interfaces&#46; Similarly&#44; the term &#34;properties&#34; is used for both JavaScript object properties and CSS properties&#46; When these are ambiguous they are qualified as <strong>object properties</strong> and <strong>CSS properties</strong> respectively&#46;

Generally&#44; when the specification states that a feature applies to <a id="terminology&#58;syntax"></a>[the HTML syntax](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#syntax) or <a id="terminology&#58;the&#45;xhtml&#45;syntax"></a>[the XML syntax](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#the-xhtml-syntax)&#44; it also includes the other&#46; When a feature specifically only applies to one of the two languages&#44; it is called out by explicitly stating that it does not apply to the other format&#44; as in &#34;for HTML&#44; &#46;&#46;&#46; &#40;this does not apply to XML&#41;&#34;&#46;

This specification uses the term <strong>document</strong> to refer to any use of HTML&#44; ranging from short static documents to long essays or reports with rich multimedia&#44; as well as to fully&#45;fledged interactive applications&#46; The term is used to refer both to <a id="terminology&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> objects and their descendant DOM trees&#44; and to serialized byte streams using the <a id="terminology&#58;syntax&#45;2"></a>[HTML syntax](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#syntax) or the <a id="terminology&#58;the&#45;xhtml&#45;syntax&#45;2"></a>[XML syntax](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#the-xhtml-syntax)&#44; depending on context&#46;

In the context of the DOM structures&#44; the terms <a id="terminology&#58;html&#45;documents"></a>[HTML document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document) and <a id="terminology&#58;xml&#45;documents"></a>[XML document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-document) are used as defined in DOM&#44; and refer specifically to two different modes that <a id="terminology&#58;document&#45;2"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> objects can find themselves in&#46; [&#91;DOM&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsDOM) &#40;Such uses are always hyperlinked to their definition&#46;&#41;

In the context of byte streams&#44; the term HTML document refers to resources labeled as <a id="terminology&#58;text&#47;html"></a><code>[text&#47;html](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#text/html)</code>&#44; and the term XML document refers to resources labeled with an <a id="terminology&#58;xml&#45;mime&#45;type"></a>[XML MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-mime-type)&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

For simplicity&#44; terms such as <strong>shown</strong>&#44; <strong>displayed</strong>&#44; and <strong>visible</strong> might sometimes be used when referring to the way a document is rendered to the user&#46; These terms are not meant to imply a visual medium&#59; they must be considered to apply to other media in equivalent ways&#46;

#### <a id="parallelism"></a>2&#46;1&#46;1 Parallelism[](#parallelism)

To run steps <a id="in&#45;parallel"></a><strong>in parallel</strong> means those steps are to be run&#44; one after another&#44; at the same time as other logic in the standard &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; at the same time as the <a id="parallelism&#58;event&#45;loop"></a>[event loop](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-loop)&#41;&#46; This standard does not define the precise mechanism by which this is achieved&#44; be it time&#45;sharing cooperative multitasking&#44; fibers&#44; threads&#44; processes&#44; using different hyperthreads&#44; cores&#44; CPUs&#44; machines&#44; etc&#46; By contrast&#44; an operation that is to run <a id="immediately"></a><strong>immediately</strong> must interrupt the currently running task&#44; run itself&#44; and then resume the previously running task&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

For guidance on writing specifications that leverage parallelism&#44; see [Dealing with the event loop from other specifications](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-loop-for-spec-authors)&#46;

To avoid race conditions between different <a id="parallelism&#58;in&#45;parallel"></a>[in parallel](#in-parallel) algorithms that operate on the same data&#44; a <a id="parallelism&#58;parallel&#45;queue"></a>[parallel queue](#parallel-queue) can be used&#46;

A <a id="parallel&#45;queue"></a><strong>parallel queue</strong> represents a queue of algorithm steps that must be run in series&#46;

A <a id="parallelism&#58;parallel&#45;queue&#45;2"></a>[parallel queue](#parallel-queue) has an <a id="algorithm&#45;queue"></a><strong>algorithm queue</strong> &#40;a <a id="parallelism&#58;queue"></a>[queue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue)&#41;&#44; initially empty&#46;

To <a id="enqueue&#45;the&#45;following&#45;steps"></a><strong>enqueue steps</strong> to a <a id="parallelism&#58;parallel&#45;queue&#45;3"></a>[parallel queue](#parallel-queue)&#44; <a id="parallelism&#58;enqueue"></a>[enqueue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-enqueue) the algorithm steps to the <a id="parallelism&#58;parallel&#45;queue&#45;4"></a>[parallel queue](#parallel-queue)&#39;s <a id="parallelism&#58;algorithm&#45;queue"></a>[algorithm queue](#algorithm-queue)&#46;

To <a id="starting&#45;a&#45;new&#45;parallel&#45;queue"></a><strong>start a new parallel queue</strong>&#44; run the following steps&#58;

1.  Let <var>parallelQueue</var> be a new <a id="parallelism&#58;parallel&#45;queue&#45;5"></a>[parallel queue](#parallel-queue)&#46;

2.  Run the following steps <a id="parallelism&#58;in&#45;parallel&#45;2"></a>[in parallel](#in-parallel)&#58;

    1.  While true&#58;

        1.  Let <var>steps</var> be the result of <a id="parallelism&#58;dequeue"></a>[dequeuing](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-dequeue) from <var>parallelQueue</var>&#39;s <a id="parallelism&#58;algorithm&#45;queue&#45;2"></a>[algorithm queue](#algorithm-queue)&#46;

        2.  If <var>steps</var> is not nothing&#44; then run <var>steps</var>&#46;

        3.  <a id="parallelism&#58;assert"></a>[Assert](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert)&#58; running <var>steps</var> did not throw an exception&#44; as steps running <a id="parallelism&#58;in&#45;parallel&#45;3"></a>[in parallel](#in-parallel) are not allowed to throw&#46;

        <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

        Implementations are not expected to implement this as a continuously running loop&#46; Algorithms in standards are to be easy to understand and are not necessarily great for battery life or performance&#46;

3.  Return <var>parallelQueue</var>&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Steps running <a id="parallelism&#58;in&#45;parallel&#45;4"></a>[in parallel](#in-parallel) can themselves run other steps in <a id="parallelism&#58;in&#45;parallel&#45;5"></a>[in parallel](#in-parallel)&#46; E&#46;g&#46;&#44; inside a <a id="parallelism&#58;parallel&#45;queue&#45;6"></a>[parallel queue](#parallel-queue) it can be useful to run a series of steps in parallel with the queue&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Imagine a standard defined <var>nameList</var> &#40;a <a id="parallelism&#58;list"></a>[list](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list)&#41;&#44; along with a method to add a <var>name</var> to <var>nameList</var>&#44; unless <var>nameList</var> already <a id="parallelism&#58;list&#45;contains"></a>[contains](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain) <var>name</var>&#44; in which case it rejects&#46;

The following solution suffers from race conditions&#58;

1.  Let <var>p</var> be a new promise created in <a id="parallelism&#58;this"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="parallelism&#58;concept&#45;relevant&#45;realm"></a>[relevant realm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-relevant-realm)&#46;

2.  Let <var>global</var> be <a id="parallelism&#58;this&#45;2"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="parallelism&#58;concept&#45;relevant&#45;global"></a>[relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-relevant-global)&#46;

3.  Run the following steps <a id="parallelism&#58;in&#45;parallel&#45;6"></a>[in parallel](#in-parallel)&#58;

    1.  If <var>nameList</var> <a id="parallelism&#58;list&#45;contains&#45;2"></a>[contains](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain) <var>name</var>&#44; then <a id="parallelism&#58;queue&#45;a&#45;global&#45;task"></a>[queue a global task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#queue-a-global-task) on the <a id="parallelism&#58;dom&#45;manipulation&#45;task&#45;source"></a>[DOM manipulation task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-manipulation-task-source) given <var>global</var> to reject <var>p</var> with a <a id="parallelism&#58;typeerror"></a><code>[TypeError](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror)</code>&#44; and abort these steps&#46;

    2.  Do some potentially lengthy work&#46;

    3.  <a id="parallelism&#58;list&#45;append"></a>[Append](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append) <var>name</var> to <var>nameList</var>&#46;

    4.  <a id="parallelism&#58;queue&#45;a&#45;global&#45;task&#45;2"></a>[Queue a global task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#queue-a-global-task) on the <a id="parallelism&#58;dom&#45;manipulation&#45;task&#45;source&#45;2"></a>[DOM manipulation task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-manipulation-task-source) given <var>global</var> to resolve <var>p</var> with undefined&#46;

4.  Return <var>p</var>&#46;

Two invocations of the above could run simultaneously&#44; meaning <var>name</var> isn&#39;t in <var>nameList</var> during step 3&#46;1&#44; but it <em>might be added</em> before step 3&#46;3 runs&#44; meaning <var>name</var> ends up in <var>nameList</var> twice&#46;

Parallel queues solve this&#46; The standard would let <var>nameListQueue</var> be the result of <a id="parallelism&#58;starting&#45;a&#45;new&#45;parallel&#45;queue"></a>[starting a new parallel queue](#starting-a-new-parallel-queue) and define the name&#45;adding steps as follows&#58;

1.  Let <var>p</var> be a new promise created in <a id="parallelism&#58;this&#45;3"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="parallelism&#58;concept&#45;relevant&#45;realm&#45;2"></a>[relevant realm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-relevant-realm)&#46;

2.  Let <var>global</var> be <a id="parallelism&#58;this&#45;4"></a>[this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)&#39;s <a id="parallelism&#58;concept&#45;relevant&#45;global&#45;2"></a>[relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-relevant-global)&#46;

3.  <a id="parallelism&#58;enqueue&#45;the&#45;following&#45;steps"></a>[Enqueue the following steps](#enqueue-the-following-steps) to <var>nameListQueue</var>&#58;

    1.  If <var>nameList</var> <a id="parallelism&#58;list&#45;contains&#45;3"></a>[contains](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain) <var>name</var>&#44; then <a id="parallelism&#58;queue&#45;a&#45;global&#45;task&#45;3"></a>[queue a global task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#queue-a-global-task) on the <a id="parallelism&#58;dom&#45;manipulation&#45;task&#45;source&#45;3"></a>[DOM manipulation task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-manipulation-task-source) given <var>global</var> to reject <var>p</var> with a <a id="parallelism&#58;typeerror&#45;2"></a><code>[TypeError](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror)</code>&#44; and abort these steps&#46;

    2.  Do some potentially lengthy work&#46;

    3.  <a id="parallelism&#58;list&#45;append&#45;2"></a>[Append](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-append) <var>name</var> to <var>nameList</var>&#46;

    4.  <a id="parallelism&#58;queue&#45;a&#45;global&#45;task&#45;4"></a>[Queue a global task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#queue-a-global-task) on the <a id="parallelism&#58;dom&#45;manipulation&#45;task&#45;source&#45;4"></a>[DOM manipulation task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-manipulation-task-source) given <var>global</var> to resolve <var>p</var> with undefined&#46;

4.  Return <var>p</var>&#46;

The steps would now queue and the race is avoided&#46;

#### <a id="resources"></a>2&#46;1&#46;2 Resources[](#resources)

The specification uses the term <strong>supported</strong> when referring to whether a user agent has an implementation capable of decoding the semantics of an external resource&#46; A format or type is said to be <em>supported</em> if the implementation can process an external resource of that format or type without critical aspects of the resource being ignored&#46; Whether a specific resource is <em>supported</em> can depend on what features of the resource&#39;s format are in use&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; a PNG image would be considered to be in a supported format if its pixel data could be decoded and rendered&#44; even if&#44; unbeknownst to the implementation&#44; the image also contained animation data&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

An MPEG&#45;4 video file would not be considered to be in a supported format if the compression format used was not supported&#44; even if the implementation could determine the dimensions of the movie from the file&#39;s metadata&#46;

What some specifications&#44; in particular the HTTP specifications&#44; refer to as a <em>representation</em> is referred to in this specification as a <strong>resource</strong>&#46; [&#91;HTTP&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsHTTP)

A resource&#39;s <a id="critical&#45;subresources"></a><strong>critical subresources</strong> are those that the resource needs to have available to be correctly processed&#46; Which resources are considered critical or not is defined by the specification that defines the resource&#39;s format&#46;

For <a id="resources&#58;css&#45;style&#45;sheet"></a>[CSS style sheets](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet)&#44; we tentatively define here that their critical subresources are other style sheets imported via <code>&#64;import</code> rules&#44; including those indirectly imported by other imported style sheets&#46;

This definition is not fully interoperable&#59; furthermore&#44; some user agents seem to count resources like background images or web fonts as critical subresources&#46; Ideally&#44; the CSS Working Group would define this&#59; see [w3c&#47;csswg&#45;drafts issue &#35;1088](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/1088) to track progress on that front&#46;

#### <a id="xml"></a>2&#46;1&#46;3 XML compatibility[](#xml)

<a id="html&#45;namespace"></a>To ease migration from HTML to XML&#44; user agents conforming to this specification will place elements in HTML in the <a id="xml&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a><code>[http&#58;&#47;&#47;www&#46;w3&#46;org&#47;1999&#47;xhtml](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)</code> namespace&#44; at least for the purposes of the DOM and CSS&#46; The term &#34;<a id="html&#45;elements"></a><strong>HTML elements</strong>&#34; refers to any element in that namespace&#44; even in XML documents&#46;

Except where otherwise stated&#44; all elements defined or mentioned in this specification are in the <a id="xml&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace) &#40;&#34;<code>http&#58;&#47;&#47;www&#46;w3&#46;org&#47;1999&#47;xhtml</code>&#34;&#41;&#44; and all attributes defined or mentioned in this specification have no namespace&#46;

The term <a id="element&#45;type"></a><strong>element type</strong> is used to refer to the set of elements that have a given local name and namespace&#46; For example&#44; <a id="xml&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code> elements are elements with the element type <a id="xml&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code>&#44; meaning they have the local name &#34;<code>button</code>&#34; and &#40;implicitly as defined above&#41; the <a id="xml&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2&#45;3"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#46;

#### <a id="dom&#45;trees"></a>2&#46;1&#46;4 DOM trees[](#dom-trees)

When it is stated that some element or attribute is <a id="ignore"></a><strong>ignored</strong>&#44; or treated as some other value&#44; or handled as if it was something else&#44; this refers only to the processing of the node after it is in the DOM&#46; A user agent must not mutate the DOM in such situations&#46;

A content attribute is said to <strong>change</strong> value only if its new value is different than its previous value&#59; setting an attribute to a value it already has does not change it&#46;

The term <strong>empty</strong>&#44; when used for an attribute value&#44; <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;text"></a><code>[Text](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text)</code> node&#44; or string&#44; means that the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;length"></a>[length](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-length) of the text is zero &#40;i&#46;e&#46;&#44; not even containing <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;control"></a>[controls](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#control) or U&#43;0020 SPACE&#41;&#46;

An HTML element can have specific <a id="html&#45;element&#45;insertion&#45;steps"></a><strong>HTML element insertion steps</strong>&#44; <a id="html&#45;element&#45;post&#45;connection&#45;steps"></a><strong>HTML element post&#45;connection steps</strong>&#44; <a id="html&#45;element&#45;removing&#45;steps"></a><strong>HTML element removing steps</strong>&#44; and <a id="html&#45;element&#45;moving&#45;steps"></a><strong>HTML element moving steps</strong> all defined for the element&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;local&#45;name"></a>[local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;insert&#45;ext"></a>[insertion steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert-ext) for the HTML Standard&#44; given <var>insertedNode</var>&#44; are defined as the following&#58;

1.  If <var>insertedNode</var> is an element whose <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;namespace"></a>[namespace](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace) is the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#44; and this standard defines <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;insertion&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element insertion steps](#html-element-insertion-steps) for <var>insertedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;local&#45;name&#45;2"></a>[local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name)&#44; then run the corresponding <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;insertion&#45;steps&#45;2"></a>[HTML element insertion steps](#html-element-insertion-steps) given <var>insertedNode</var>&#46;

2.  If <var>insertedNode</var> is a <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated element](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-associated-element) or the ancestor of a <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[form&#45;associated element](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-associated-element)&#58;

    1.  If the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[form&#45;associated element](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-associated-element)&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;parser&#45;inserted&#45;flag"></a>[parser inserted flag](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#parser-inserted-flag) is set&#44; then return&#46;

    2.  <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;reset&#45;the&#45;form&#45;owner"></a>[Reset the form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#reset-the-form-owner) of the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;4"></a>[form&#45;associated element](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-associated-element)&#46;

3.  If <var>insertedNode</var> is an <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;element"></a><code>[Element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element)</code> that is not on the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;stack&#45;of&#45;open&#45;elements"></a>[stack of open elements](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#stack-of-open-elements) of an <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;parser"></a>[HTML parser](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#html-parser)&#44; then <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;process&#45;internal&#45;resource&#45;links"></a>[process internal resource links](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#process-internal-resource-links) given <var>insertedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;node&#45;document"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;post&#45;connection&#45;ext"></a>[post&#45;connection steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-post-connection-ext) for the HTML Standard&#44; given <var>insertedNode</var>&#44; are defined as the following&#58;

1.  If <var>insertedNode</var> is an element whose <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a>[namespace](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace) is the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#44; and this standard defines <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;post&#45;connection&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element post&#45;connection steps](#html-element-post-connection-steps) for <var>insertedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;local&#45;name&#45;3"></a>[local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name)&#44; then run the corresponding <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;post&#45;connection&#45;steps&#45;2"></a>[HTML element post&#45;connection steps](#html-element-post-connection-steps) given <var>insertedNode</var>&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;remove&#45;ext"></a>[removing steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove-ext) for the HTML Standard&#44; given <var>removedNode</var>&#44; <var>isSubtreeRoot</var>&#44; and <var>oldAncestor</var>&#44; are defined as the following&#58;

1.  Let <var>document</var> be <var>removedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;node&#45;document&#45;2"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#46;

2.  <a id="node&#45;remove&#45;focus&#45;fixup"></a>

    If <var>document</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;focused&#45;area&#45;of&#45;the&#45;document"></a>[focused area](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focused-area-of-the-document) is <var>removedNode</var>&#44; then set <var>document</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;focused&#45;area&#45;of&#45;the&#45;document&#45;2"></a>[focused area](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focused-area-of-the-document) to <var>document</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;viewport"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#44; and set <var>document</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;relevant&#45;global"></a>[relevant global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-relevant-global)&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;window&#45;navigation&#45;api"></a>[navigation API](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#window-navigation-api)&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;focus&#45;changed&#45;during&#45;ongoing&#45;navigation"></a>[focus changed during ongoing navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#focus-changed-during-ongoing-navigation) to false&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    This does <em>not</em> perform the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;unfocusing&#45;steps"></a>[unfocusing steps](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#unfocusing-steps)&#44; <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;focusing&#45;steps"></a>[focusing steps](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focusing-steps)&#44; or <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;focus&#45;update&#45;steps"></a>[focus update steps](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focus-update-steps)&#44; and thus no <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;event&#45;blur"></a><code>[blur](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-blur)</code> or <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;event&#45;change"></a><code>[change](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-change)</code> events are fired&#46;

3.  If <var>removedNode</var> is an element whose <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;namespace&#45;3"></a>[namespace](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace) is the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2&#45;3"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#44; and this standard defines <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;removing&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element removing steps](#html-element-removing-steps) for <var>removedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;local&#45;name&#45;4"></a>[local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name)&#44; then run the corresponding <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;removing&#45;steps&#45;2"></a>[HTML element removing steps](#html-element-removing-steps) given <var>removedNode</var>&#44; <var>isSubtreeRoot</var>&#44; and <var>oldAncestor</var>&#46;

4.  If <var>removedNode</var> is a <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;5"></a>[form&#45;associated element](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-associated-element) with a non&#45;null <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;owner"></a>[form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-owner) and <var>removedNode</var> and its <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;2"></a>[form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-owner) are no longer in the same <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;tree"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree)&#44; then <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;reset&#45;the&#45;form&#45;owner&#45;2"></a>[reset the form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#reset-the-form-owner) of <var>removedNode</var>&#46;

5.  If <var>removedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;attr&#45;popover"></a><code>[popover](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-popover)</code> attribute is not in the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;attr&#45;popover&#45;none&#45;state"></a>[No Popover](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-popover-none-state) state&#44; then run the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;hide&#45;popover&#45;algorithm"></a>[hide popover algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#hide-popover-algorithm) given <var>removedNode</var>&#44; false&#44; false&#44; false&#44; and null&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;move&#45;ext"></a>[moving steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-move-ext) for the HTML Standard&#44; given <var>movedNode</var>&#44; <var>isSubtreeRoot</var>&#44; and <var>oldAncestor</var>&#44; are defined as the following&#58;

1.  If <var>movedNode</var> is an element whose <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;namespace&#45;4"></a>[namespace](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-namespace) is the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2&#45;4"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#44; and this standard defines <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;moving&#45;steps"></a>[HTML element moving steps](#html-element-moving-steps) for <var>movedNode</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;local&#45;name&#45;5"></a>[local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-local-name)&#44; then run the corresponding <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;html&#45;element&#45;moving&#45;steps&#45;2"></a>[HTML element moving steps](#html-element-moving-steps) given <var>movedNode</var>&#44; <var>isSubtreeRoot</var>&#44; and <var>oldAncestor</var>&#46;

2.  If <var>movedNode</var> is a <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element&#45;6"></a>[form&#45;associated element](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-associated-element) with a non&#45;null <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;3"></a>[form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-owner) and <var>movedNode</var> and its <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;form&#45;owner&#45;4"></a>[form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-owner) are no longer in the same <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;tree&#45;2"></a>[tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree)&#44; then <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;reset&#45;the&#45;form&#45;owner&#45;3"></a>[reset the form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#reset-the-form-owner) of <var>movedNode</var>&#46;

A <a id="insert&#45;an&#45;element&#45;into&#45;a&#45;document"></a><strong>node is inserted into a document</strong> when the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;insert&#45;ext&#45;2"></a>[insertion steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert-ext) are invoked with it as the argument and it is now <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;in&#45;a&#45;document&#45;tree"></a>[in a document tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree)&#46; Analogously&#44; a <a id="remove&#45;an&#45;element&#45;from&#45;a&#45;document"></a><strong>node is removed from a document</strong> when the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;remove&#45;ext&#45;2"></a>[removing steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove-ext) are invoked with it as the argument and it is now no longer <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;in&#45;a&#45;document&#45;tree&#45;2"></a>[in a document tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree)&#46;

A node <a id="becomes&#45;connected"></a><strong>becomes connected</strong> when the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;insert&#45;ext&#45;3"></a>[insertion steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert-ext) are invoked with it as the argument and it is now <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;connected"></a>[connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected)&#46; Analogously&#44; a node <a id="becomes&#45;disconnected"></a><strong>becomes disconnected</strong> when the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;remove&#45;ext&#45;3"></a>[removing steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove-ext) are invoked with it as the argument and it is now no longer <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;connected&#45;2"></a>[connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected)&#46;

A node is <a id="browsing&#45;context&#45;connected"></a><strong>browsing&#45;context connected</strong> when it is <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;connected&#45;3"></a>[connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected) and its <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;shadow&#45;including&#45;root"></a>[shadow&#45;including root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-root)&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;bc"></a>[browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-document-bc) is non&#45;null&#46; A node <a id="becomes&#45;browsing&#45;context&#45;connected"></a><strong>becomes browsing&#45;context connected</strong> when the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;insert&#45;ext&#45;4"></a>[insertion steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert-ext) are invoked with it as the argument and it is now <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;browsing&#45;context&#45;connected"></a>[browsing&#45;context connected](#browsing-context-connected)&#46; A node <a id="becomes&#45;browsing&#45;context&#45;disconnected"></a><strong>becomes browsing&#45;context disconnected</strong> either when the <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;remove&#45;ext&#45;4"></a>[removing steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove-ext) are invoked with it as the argument and it is now no longer <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;browsing&#45;context&#45;connected&#45;2"></a>[browsing&#45;context connected](#browsing-context-connected)&#44; or when its <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;shadow&#45;including&#45;root&#45;2"></a>[shadow&#45;including root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-root)&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;trees&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;bc&#45;2"></a>[browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-document-bc) becomes null&#46;

#### <a id="scripting&#45;2"></a>2&#46;1&#46;5 Scripting[](#scripting-2)

The construction &#34;a <code>Foo</code> object&#34;&#44; where <code>Foo</code> is actually an interface&#44; is sometimes used instead of the more accurate &#34;an object implementing the interface <code>Foo</code>&#34;&#46;

An IDL attribute is said to be <strong>getting</strong> when its value is being retrieved &#40;e&#46;g&#46; by author script&#41;&#44; and is said to be <strong>setting</strong> when a new value is assigned to it&#46;

If a DOM object is said to be <a id="live"></a><strong>live</strong>&#44; then the attributes and methods on that object must operate on the actual underlying data&#44; not a snapshot of the data&#46;

#### <a id="plugins"></a>2&#46;1&#46;6 Plugins[](#plugins)

The term <a id="plugin"></a><strong>plugin</strong> refers to an <a id="plugins&#58;implementation&#45;defined"></a>[implementation&#45;defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined) set of content handlers used by the user agent that can take part in the user agent&#39;s rendering of a <a id="plugins&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> object&#44; but that neither act as <a id="plugins&#58;child&#45;navigable"></a>[child navigables](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#child-navigable) of the <a id="plugins&#58;document&#45;2"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> nor introduce any <a id="plugins&#58;node"></a><code>[Node](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-node)</code> objects to the <a id="plugins&#58;document&#45;3"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code>&#39;s DOM&#46;

Typically such content handlers are provided by third parties&#44; though a user agent can also designate built&#45;in content handlers as plugins&#46;

A user agent must not consider the types <a id="plugins&#58;text&#47;plain"></a><code>[text&#47;plain](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)</code> and <a id="plugins&#58;application&#47;octet&#45;stream"></a><code>[application&#47;octet&#45;stream](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1)</code> as having a registered <a id="plugins&#58;plugin"></a>[plugin](#plugin)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

One example of a plugin would be a PDF viewer that is instantiated in a <a id="plugins&#58;navigable"></a>[navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#navigable) when the user navigates to a PDF file&#46; This would count as a plugin regardless of whether the party that implemented the PDF viewer component was the same as that which implemented the user agent itself&#46; However&#44; a PDF viewer application that launches separate from the user agent &#40;as opposed to using the same interface&#41; is not a plugin by this definition&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This specification does not define a mechanism for interacting with plugins&#44; as it is expected to be user&#45;agent&#45; and platform&#45;specific&#46; Some UAs might opt to support a plugin mechanism such as the Netscape Plugin API&#59; others might use remote content converters or have built&#45;in support for certain types&#46; Indeed&#44; this specification doesn&#39;t require user agents to support plugins at all&#46; [&#91;NPAPI&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsNPAPI)

<strong>Warning&#58;</strong>

Browsers should take extreme care when interacting with external content intended for <a id="plugins&#58;plugin&#45;2"></a>[plugins](#plugin)&#46; When third&#45;party software is run with the same privileges as the user agent itself&#44; vulnerabilities in the third&#45;party software become as dangerous as those in the user agent&#46;

<a id="plugins&#58;tracking&#45;vector"></a>[![&#40;This is a tracking vector&#46;&#41;](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#tracking-vector) Since different users having different sets of <a id="plugins&#58;plugin&#45;3"></a>[plugins](#plugin) provides a tracking vector that increases the chances of users being uniquely identified&#44; user agents are encouraged to support the exact same set of <a id="plugins&#58;plugin&#45;4"></a>[plugins](#plugin) for each user&#46;

#### <a id="encoding&#45;terminology"></a>2&#46;1&#46;7 Character encodings[](#encoding-terminology)

A <a id="encoding"></a><strong>[character encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding)</strong>&#44; or just <em>encoding</em> where that is not ambiguous&#44; is a defined way to convert between byte streams and Unicode strings&#44; as defined in Encoding&#46; An <a id="encoding&#45;terminology&#58;encoding"></a>[encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) has an <a id="encoding&#45;name"></a><strong>[encoding name](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#name)</strong> and one or more <a id="encoding&#45;label"></a><strong>[encoding labels](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#label)</strong>&#44; referred to as the encoding&#39;s <em>name</em> and <em>labels</em> in the Encoding standard&#46; [&#91;ENCODING&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsENCODING)

#### <a id="conformance&#45;classes"></a>2&#46;1&#46;8 Conformance classes[](#conformance-classes)

This specification describes the conformance criteria for user agents &#40;relevant to implementers&#41; and documents &#40;relevant to authors and authoring tool implementers&#41;&#46;

<a id="conforming&#45;documents"></a><strong>Conforming documents</strong> are those that comply with all the conformance criteria for documents&#46; For readability&#44; some of these conformance requirements are phrased as conformance requirements on authors&#59; such requirements are implicitly requirements on documents&#58; by definition&#44; all documents are assumed to have had an author&#46; &#40;In some cases&#44; that author may itself be a user agent — such user agents are subject to additional rules&#44; as explained below&#46;&#41;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; if a requirement states that &#34;authors must not use the <code>foobar</code> element&#34;&#44; it would imply that documents are not allowed to contain elements named <code>foobar</code>&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

There is no implied relationship between document conformance requirements and implementation conformance requirements&#46; User agents are not free to handle non&#45;conformant documents as they please&#59; the processing model described in this specification applies to implementations regardless of the conformity of the input documents&#46;

User agents fall into several &#40;overlapping&#41; categories with different conformance requirements&#46;

<a id="interactive"></a><strong>Web browsers and other interactive user agents</strong>

Web browsers that support <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;xhtml&#45;syntax"></a>[the XML syntax](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#the-xhtml-syntax) must process elements and attributes from the <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace) found in XML documents as described in this specification&#44; so that users can interact with them&#44; unless the semantics of those elements have been overridden by other specifications&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

A conforming web browser would&#44; upon finding a <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> element in an XML document&#44; execute the script contained in that element&#46; However&#44; if the element is found within a transformation expressed in XSLT &#40;assuming the user agent also supports XSLT&#41;&#44; then the processor would instead treat the <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> element as an opaque element that forms part of the transform&#46;

Web browsers that support <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;syntax"></a>[the HTML syntax](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#syntax) must process documents labeled with an <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;html&#45;mime&#45;type"></a>[HTML MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#html-mime-type) as described in this specification&#44; so that users can interact with them&#46;

User agents that support scripting must also be conforming implementations of the IDL fragments in this specification&#44; as described in Web IDL&#46; [&#91;WEBIDL&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsWEBIDL)

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Unless explicitly stated&#44; specifications that override the semantics of HTML elements do not override the requirements on DOM objects representing those elements&#46; For example&#44; the <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> element in the example above would still implement the <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;htmlscriptelement"></a><code>[HTMLScriptElement](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#htmlscriptelement)</code> interface&#46;

<a id="non&#45;interactive"></a><strong>Non&#45;interactive presentation user agents</strong>

User agents that process HTML and XML documents purely to render non&#45;interactive versions of them must comply to the same conformance criteria as web browsers&#44; except that they are exempt from requirements regarding user interaction&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Typical examples of non&#45;interactive presentation user agents are printers &#40;static UAs&#41; and overhead displays &#40;dynamic UAs&#41;&#46; It is expected that most static non&#45;interactive presentation user agents will also opt to [lack scripting support](#non-scripted)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

A non&#45;interactive but dynamic presentation UA would still execute scripts&#44; allowing forms to be dynamically submitted&#44; and so forth&#46; However&#44; since the concept of &#34;focus&#34; is irrelevant when the user cannot interact with the document&#44; the UA would not need to support any of the focus&#45;related DOM APIs&#46;

<a id="renderingUA"></a><strong>Visual user agents that support the suggested default rendering</strong>

User agents&#44; whether interactive or not&#44; may be designated &#40;possibly as a user option&#41; as supporting the suggested default rendering defined by this specification&#46;

This is not required&#46; In particular&#44; even user agents that do implement the suggested default rendering are encouraged to offer settings that override this default to improve the experience for the user&#44; e&#46;g&#46; changing the color contrast&#44; using different focus styles&#44; or otherwise making the experience more accessible and usable to the user&#46;

User agents that are designated as supporting the suggested default rendering must&#44; while so designated&#44; implement the rules [the Rendering section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#rendering) defines as the behavior that user agents are <em>expected</em> to implement&#46;

<a id="non&#45;scripted"></a><strong>User agents with no scripting support</strong>

Implementations that do not support scripting &#40;or which have their scripting features disabled entirely&#41; are exempt from supporting the events and DOM interfaces mentioned in this specification&#46; For the parts of this specification that are defined in terms of an events model or in terms of the DOM&#44; such user agents must still act as if events and the DOM were supported&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Scripting can form an integral part of an application&#46; Web browsers that do not support scripting&#44; or that have scripting disabled&#44; might be unable to fully convey the author&#39;s intent&#46;

<strong>Conformance checkers</strong>

<a id="conformance&#45;checkers"></a>

Conformance checkers must verify that a document conforms to the applicable conformance criteria described in this specification&#46; Automated conformance checkers are exempt from detecting errors that require interpretation of the author&#39;s intent &#40;for example&#44; while a document is non&#45;conforming if the content of a <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;blockquote&#45;element"></a><code>[blockquote](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-blockquote-element)</code> element is not a quote&#44; conformance checkers running without the input of human judgement do not have to check that <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;blockquote&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[blockquote](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-blockquote-element)</code> elements only contain quoted material&#41;&#46;

Conformance checkers must check that the input document conforms when parsed without a <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;bc"></a>[browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-document-bc) &#40;meaning that no scripts are run&#44; and that the parser&#39;s <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;scripting&#45;mode"></a>[scripting mode](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#scripting-mode) is <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;scripting&#45;mode&#45;disabled"></a>[Disabled](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#scripting-mode-disabled)&#41;&#44; and should also check that the input document conforms when parsed with a <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;bc&#45;2"></a>[browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-document-bc) in which scripts execute&#44; and that the scripts never cause non&#45;conforming states to occur other than transiently during script execution itself&#46; &#40;This is only a &#34;SHOULD&#34; and not a &#34;MUST&#34; requirement because it has been proven to be impossible&#46; [&#91;COMPUTABLE&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCOMPUTABLE)&#41;

The term &#34;HTML validator&#34; can be used to refer to a conformance checker that itself conforms to the applicable requirements of this specification&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

XML DTDs cannot express all the conformance requirements of this specification&#46; Therefore&#44; a validating XML processor and a DTD cannot constitute a conformance checker&#46; Also&#44; since neither of the two authoring formats defined in this specification are applications of SGML&#44; a validating SGML system cannot constitute a conformance checker either&#46;

To put it another way&#44; there are three types of conformance criteria&#58;

1.  Criteria that can be expressed in a DTD&#46;
2.  Criteria that cannot be expressed by a DTD&#44; but can still be checked by a machine&#46;
3.  Criteria that can only be checked by a human&#46;

A conformance checker must check for the first two&#46; A simple DTD&#45;based validator only checks for the first class of errors and is therefore not a conforming conformance checker according to this specification&#46;

<strong>Data mining tools</strong>

<a id="data&#45;mining"></a>

Applications and tools that process HTML and XML documents for reasons other than to either render the documents or check them for conformance should act in accordance with the semantics of the documents that they process&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

A tool that generates <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;outline"></a>[document outlines](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#outline) but increases the nesting level for each paragraph and does not increase the nesting level for <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;concept&#45;heading"></a>[headings](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#concept-heading) would not be conforming&#46;

<a id="editors"></a><strong>Authoring tools and markup generators</strong>

Authoring tools and markup generators must generate <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;conforming&#45;documents"></a>[conforming documents](#conforming-documents)&#46; Conformance criteria that apply to authors also apply to authoring tools&#44; where appropriate&#46;

Authoring tools are exempt from the strict requirements of using elements only for their specified purpose&#44; but only to the extent that authoring tools are not yet able to determine author intent&#46; However&#44; authoring tools must not automatically misuse elements or encourage their users to do so&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; it is not conforming to use an <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;address&#45;element"></a><code>[address](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-address-element)</code> element for arbitrary contact information&#59; that element can only be used for marking up contact information for its nearest <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;article&#45;element"></a><code>[article](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-article-element)</code> or <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;body&#45;element"></a><code>[body](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-body-element)</code> element ancestor&#46; However&#44; since an authoring tool is likely unable to determine the difference&#44; an authoring tool is exempt from that requirement&#46; This does not mean&#44; though&#44; that authoring tools can use <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;address&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[address](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-address-element)</code> elements for any block of italics text &#40;for instance&#41;&#59; it just means that the authoring tool doesn&#39;t have to verify that when the user uses a tool for inserting contact information for an <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;article&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[article](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-article-element)</code> element&#44; that the user really is doing that and not inserting something else instead&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

In terms of conformance checking&#44; an editor has to output documents that conform to the same extent that a conformance checker will verify&#46;

When an authoring tool is used to edit a non&#45;conforming document&#44; it may preserve the conformance errors in sections of the document that were not edited during the editing session &#40;i&#46;e&#46;&#44; an editing tool is allowed to roundtrip erroneous content&#41;&#46; However&#44; an authoring tool must not claim that the output is conformant if errors have been so preserved&#46;

Authoring tools are expected to come in two broad varieties&#58; tools that work from structure or semantic data&#44; and tools that work on a What&#45;You&#45;See&#45;Is&#45;What&#45;You&#45;Get media&#45;specific editing basis &#40;WYSIWYG&#41;&#46;

The former is the preferred mechanism for tools that author HTML&#44; since the structure in the source information can be used to make informed choices regarding which HTML elements and attributes are most appropriate&#46;

However&#44; WYSIWYG tools are legitimate&#46; WYSIWYG tools should use elements they know are appropriate&#44; and should not use elements that they do not know to be appropriate&#46; This might in certain extreme cases mean limiting the use of flow elements to just a few elements&#44; like <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;div&#45;element"></a><code>[div](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-div-element)</code>&#44; <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;b&#45;element"></a><code>[b](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-b-element)</code>&#44; <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;i&#45;element"></a><code>[i](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-i-element)</code>&#44; and <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;span&#45;element"></a><code>[span](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-span-element)</code> and making liberal use of the <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;attr&#45;style"></a><code>[style](#attr-style)</code> attribute&#46;

All authoring tools&#44; whether WYSIWYG or not&#44; should make a best effort attempt at enabling users to create well&#45;structured&#44; semantically rich&#44; media&#45;independent content&#46;

For compatibility with existing content and prior specifications&#44; this specification describes two authoring formats&#58; one based on <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;the&#45;xhtml&#45;syntax&#45;2"></a>[XML](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#the-xhtml-syntax)&#44; and one using a [custom format](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#writing) inspired by SGML &#40;referred to as <a id="conformance&#45;classes&#58;syntax&#45;2"></a>[the HTML syntax](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#syntax)&#41;&#46; Implementations must support at least one of these two formats&#44; although supporting both is encouraged&#46;

Some conformance requirements are phrased as requirements on elements&#44; attributes&#44; methods or objects&#46; Such requirements fall into two categories&#58; those describing content model restrictions&#44; and those describing implementation behavior&#46; Those in the former category are requirements on documents and authoring tools&#46; Those in the second category are requirements on user agents&#46; Similarly&#44; some conformance requirements are phrased as requirements on authors&#59; such requirements are to be interpreted as conformance requirements on the documents that authors produce&#46; &#40;In other words&#44; this specification does not distinguish between conformance criteria on authors and conformance criteria on documents&#46;&#41;

<strong>Unicode and Encoding</strong>

The Unicode character set is used to represent textual data&#44; and Encoding defines requirements around <a id="dependencies&#58;encoding"></a>[character encodings](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding)&#46; [&#91;UNICODE&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsUNICODE)

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This specification [introduces terminology](#encoding-terminology) based on the terms defined in those specifications&#44; as described earlier&#46;

The following terms are used as defined in Encoding&#58; [&#91;ENCODING&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsENCODING)

- <a id="getting&#45;an&#45;encoding"></a><strong>[Getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get)</strong>
- <a id="get&#45;an&#45;output&#45;encoding"></a><strong>[Get an output encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#get-an-output-encoding)</strong>
- The generic <a id="decode"></a><strong>[decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode)</strong> algorithm which takes a byte stream and an encoding and returns a character stream
- The <a id="utf&#45;8&#45;decode"></a><strong>[UTF&#45;8 decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode)</strong> algorithm which takes a byte stream and returns a character stream&#44; additionally stripping one leading UTF&#45;8 Byte Order Mark &#40;BOM&#41;&#44; if any
- The <a id="utf&#45;8&#45;decode&#45;without&#45;bom"></a><strong>[UTF&#45;8 decode without BOM](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode-without-bom)</strong> algorithm which is identical to <a id="dependencies&#58;utf&#45;8&#45;decode"></a>[UTF&#45;8 decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) except that it does not strip one leading UTF&#45;8 Byte Order Mark &#40;BOM&#41;
- The <a id="encode"></a><strong>[encode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encode)</strong> algorithm which takes a character stream and an encoding and returns a byte stream
- The <a id="utf&#45;8&#45;encode"></a><strong>[UTF&#45;8 encode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encode)</strong> algorithm which takes a character stream and returns a byte stream
- The <a id="bom&#45;sniff"></a><strong>[BOM sniff](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#bom-sniff)</strong> algorithm which takes a byte stream and returns an encoding or null&#46;

<strong>XML and related specifications</strong>

Implementations that support <a id="dependencies&#58;the&#45;xhtml&#45;syntax"></a>[the XML syntax](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#the-xhtml-syntax) for HTML must support some version of XML&#44; as well as its corresponding namespaces specification&#44; because that syntax uses an XML serialization with namespaces&#46; [&#91;XML&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXML) [&#91;XMLNS&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXMLNS)

Data mining tools and other user agents that perform operations on content without running scripts&#44; evaluating CSS or XPath expressions&#44; or otherwise exposing the resulting DOM to arbitrary content&#44; may &#34;support namespaces&#34; by just asserting that their DOM node analogues are in certain namespaces&#44; without actually exposing the namespace strings&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

In <a id="dependencies&#58;syntax"></a>[the HTML syntax](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#syntax)&#44; namespace prefixes and namespace declarations do not have the same effect as in XML&#46; For instance&#44; the colon has no special meaning in HTML element names&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The attribute with the name <a id="attr&#45;xml&#45;space"></a><strong>[<code>space</code>](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-white-space)</strong> in the <a id="dependencies&#58;xml&#45;namespace"></a>[XML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-namespace) is defined by Extensible Markup Language &#40;XML&#41;&#46; [&#91;XML&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXML)

The <a id="xml&#45;name"></a><strong>[<code>Name</code>](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#NT-Name)</strong> production is defined in XML&#46; [&#91;XML&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXML)

This specification also references the <a id="xml&#45;stylesheet"></a><strong>[<code>&#60;&#63;xml&#45;stylesheet&#63;&#62;</code>](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-stylesheet/#the-xml-stylesheet-processing-instruction)</strong> processing instruction&#44; defined in Associating Style Sheets with XML documents&#46; [&#91;XMLSSPI&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXMLSSPI)

This specification also non&#45;normatively mentions the <a id="xsltprocessor"></a><strong><code>XSLTProcessor</code></strong> interface and its <a id="dom&#45;xsltprocessor&#45;transformtofragment"></a><strong><code>transformToFragment&#40;&#41;</code></strong> and <a id="dom&#45;xsltprocessor&#45;transformtodocument"></a><strong><code>transformToDocument&#40;&#41;</code></strong> methods&#46; [&#91;XSLTP&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXSLTP)

When this specification requires a user agent to <a id="create&#45;a&#45;date&#45;object"></a><strong>create a <code>Date</code> object</strong> representing a particular time &#40;which could be the special value Not&#45;a&#45;Number&#41;&#44; the milliseconds component of that time&#44; if any&#44; must be truncated to an integer&#44; and the time value of the newly created <a id="dependencies&#58;date"></a><code>[Date](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects)</code> object must represent the resulting truncated time&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For instance&#44; given the time 23045 millionths of a second after 01&#58;00 UTC on January 1st 2000&#44; i&#46;e&#46; the time 2000&#45;01&#45;01T00&#58;00&#58;00&#46;023045Z&#44; then the <a id="dependencies&#58;date&#45;2"></a><code>[Date](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects)</code> object created representing that time would represent the same time as that created representing the time 2000&#45;01&#45;01T00&#58;00&#58;00&#46;023Z&#44; 45 millionths earlier&#46; If the given time is NaN&#44; then the result is a <a id="dependencies&#58;date&#45;3"></a><code>[Date](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects)</code> object that represents a time value NaN &#40;indicating that the object does not represent a specific instant of time&#41;&#46;

<strong>JavaScript</strong>

Some parts of the language described by this specification only support JavaScript as the underlying scripting language&#46; [&#91;JAVASCRIPT&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsJAVASCRIPT)

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The term &#34;JavaScript&#34; is used to refer to ECMA&#45;262&#44; rather than the official term ECMAScript&#44; since the term JavaScript is more widely known&#46;

The following terms are defined in the JavaScript specification and used in this specification&#58;

- <a id="early&#45;error"></a><strong>[early error](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#early-error-rule)</strong>

<strong>DOM</strong>

The Document Object Model &#40;DOM&#41; is a representation — a model — of a document and its content&#46; The DOM is not just an API&#59; the conformance criteria of HTML implementations are defined&#44; in this specification&#44; in terms of operations on the DOM&#46; [&#91;DOM&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsDOM)

Implementations must support DOM and the events defined in UI Events&#44; because this specification is defined in terms of the DOM&#44; and some of the features are defined as extensions to the DOM interfaces&#46; [&#91;DOM&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsDOM) [&#91;UIEVENTS&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsUIEVENTS)

In particular&#44; the following features are defined in DOM&#58; [&#91;DOM&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsDOM)

<strong>CSS modules</strong>

While support for CSS as a whole is not required of implementations of this specification &#40;though it is encouraged&#44; at least for web browsers&#41;&#44; some features are defined in terms of specific CSS requirements&#46;

When this specification requires that something be <a id="parse&#45;something&#45;according&#45;to&#45;a&#45;css&#45;grammar"></a><strong>[parsed according to a particular CSS grammar](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar)</strong>&#44; the relevant algorithm in CSS Syntax must be followed&#44; including error handling rules&#46; [&#91;CSSSYNTAX&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSSSYNTAX)

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; user agents are required to close all open constructs upon finding the end of a style sheet unexpectedly&#46; Thus&#44; when parsing the string &#34;<code>rgb&#40;0&#44;0&#44;0</code>&#34; &#40;with a missing close&#45;parenthesis&#41; for a color value&#44; the close parenthesis is implied by this error handling rule&#44; and a value is obtained &#40;the color &#39;black&#39;&#41;&#46; However&#44; the similar construct &#34;<code>rgb&#40;0&#44;0&#44;</code>&#34; &#40;with both a missing parenthesis and a missing &#34;blue&#34; value&#41; cannot be parsed&#44; as closing the open construct does not result in a viable value&#46;

The following terms and features are defined in Cascading Style Sheets &#40;CSS&#41;&#58; [&#91;CSS&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSS)

<strong>SVG</strong>

While support for SVG as a whole is not required by this specification &#40;though it is encouraged&#44; at least for web browsers&#41;&#44; certain features depend upon parts of SVG being implemented&#46;

User agents that implement SVG must implement the SVG 2 specification&#44; and not any earlier revisions&#46;

This specification does not <em>require</em> support of any particular network protocol&#44; style sheet language&#44; scripting language&#44; or any of the DOM specifications beyond those required in the list above&#46; However&#44; the language described by this specification is biased towards CSS as the styling language&#44; JavaScript as the scripting language&#44; and HTTP as the network protocol&#44; and several features assume that those languages and protocols are in use&#46;

A user agent that implements the HTTP protocol must implement HTTP State Management Mechanism &#40;Cookies&#41; as well&#46; [&#91;HTTP&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsHTTP) [&#91;COOKIES&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCOOKIES)

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This specification might have certain additional requirements on character encodings&#44; image formats&#44; audio formats&#44; and video formats in the respective sections&#46;

#### <a id="extensibility&#45;2"></a>2&#46;1&#46;10 Extensibility[](#extensibility-2)

Vendor&#45;specific proprietary user agent extensions to this specification are strongly discouraged&#46; Documents must not use such extensions&#44; as doing so reduces interoperability and fragments the user base&#44; allowing only users of specific user agents to access the content in question&#46;

All extensions must be defined so that the use of extensions neither contradicts nor causes the non&#45;conformance of functionality defined in the specification&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; while strongly discouraged from doing so&#44; an implementation could add a new IDL attribute &#34;<code>typeTime</code>&#34; to a control that returned the time it took the user to select the current value of a control &#40;say&#41;&#46; On the other hand&#44; defining a new control that appears in a form&#39;s <a id="extensibility&#45;2&#58;dom&#45;form&#45;elements"></a><code>[elements](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#dom-form-elements)</code> array would be in violation of the above requirement&#44; as it would violate the definition of <a id="extensibility&#45;2&#58;dom&#45;form&#45;elements&#45;2"></a><code>[elements](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#dom-form-elements)</code> given in this specification&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

When vendor&#45;neutral extensions to this specification are needed&#44; either this specification can be updated accordingly&#44; or an extension specification can be written that overrides the requirements in this specification&#46; When someone applying this specification to their activities decides that they will recognize the requirements of such an extension specification&#44; it becomes an <a id="other&#45;applicable&#45;specifications"></a><strong>applicable specification</strong> for the purposes of conformance requirements in this specification&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Someone could write a specification that defines any arbitrary byte stream as conforming&#44; and then claim that their random junk is conforming&#46; However&#44; that does not mean that their random junk actually is conforming for everyone&#39;s purposes&#58; if someone else decides that that specification does not apply to their work&#44; then they can quite legitimately say that the aforementioned random junk is just that&#44; junk&#44; and not conforming at all&#46; As far as conformance goes&#44; what matters in a particular community is what that community <em>agrees</em> is applicable&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

User agents must treat elements and attributes that they do not understand as semantically neutral&#59; leaving them in the DOM &#40;for DOM processors&#41;&#44; and styling them according to CSS &#40;for CSS processors&#41;&#44; but not inferring any meaning from them&#46;

When support for a feature is disabled &#40;e&#46;g&#46; as an emergency measure to mitigate a security problem&#44; or to aid in development&#44; or for performance reasons&#41;&#44; user agents must act as if they had no support for the feature whatsoever&#44; and as if the feature was not mentioned in this specification&#46; For example&#44; if a particular feature is accessed via an attribute in a Web IDL interface&#44; the attribute itself would be omitted from the objects that implement that interface — leaving the attribute on the object but making it return null or throw an exception is insufficient&#46;

#### <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt"></a>2&#46;1&#46;11 Interactions with XPath and XSLT[](#interactions-with-xpath-and-xslt)

Avoid using client&#45;side XSLT in browsers&#46; The browser implementations of XSLT are highly susceptible to memory safety vulnerabilities&#44; and the web platform has evolved toward JavaScript as the safe replacement&#46; For these reasons&#44; this feature is in the process of being removed from the web platform&#46; &#40;This is a long process that takes many years&#46;&#41;

<a id="xpath&#45;1&#46;0&#45;processors"></a>Implementations of XPath 1&#46;0 that operate on <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;html&#45;documents"></a>[HTML documents](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document) parsed or created in the manners described in this specification &#40;e&#46;g&#46; as part of the <code>document&#46;evaluate&#40;&#41;</code> API&#41; must act as if the following edit was applied to the XPath 1&#46;0 specification&#46;

First&#44; remove this paragraph&#58;

> A [QName](https://www.w3.org/TR/REC-xml-names/#NT-QName) in the node test is expanded into an [expanded&#45;name](https://www.w3.org/TR/1999/REC-xpath-19991116/#dt-expanded-name) using the namespace declarations from the expression context&#46; This is the same way expansion is done for element type names in start and end&#45;tags except that the default namespace declared with <code>xmlns</code> is not used&#58; if the [QName](https://www.w3.org/TR/REC-xml-names/#NT-QName) does not have a prefix&#44; then the namespace URI is null &#40;this is the same way attribute names are expanded&#41;&#46; It is an error if the [QName](https://www.w3.org/TR/REC-xml-names/#NT-QName) has a prefix for which there is no namespace declaration in the expression context&#46;

Then&#44; insert in its place the following&#58;

> A QName in the node test is expanded into an expanded&#45;name using the namespace declarations from the expression context&#46; If the QName has a prefix&#44; then there must be a namespace declaration for this prefix in the expression context&#44; and the corresponding namespace URI is the one that is associated with this prefix&#46; It is an error if the QName has a prefix for which there is no namespace declaration in the expression context&#46;
>
> If the QName has no prefix and the principal node type of the axis is element&#44; then the default element namespace is used&#46; Otherwise&#44; if the QName has no prefix&#44; the namespace URI is null&#46; The default element namespace is a member of the context for the XPath expression&#46; The value of the default element namespace when executing an XPath expression through the DOM3 XPath API is determined in the following way&#58;
>
> 1.  If the context node is from an HTML DOM&#44; the default element namespace is &#34;http&#58;&#47;&#47;www&#46;w3&#46;org&#47;1999&#47;xhtml&#34;&#46;
> 2.  Otherwise&#44; the default element namespace URI is null&#46;
>
> <strong>Note&#58;</strong>
>
> This is equivalent to adding the default element namespace feature of XPath 2&#46;0 to XPath 1&#46;0&#44; and using the HTML namespace as the default element namespace for HTML documents&#46; It is motivated by the desire to have implementations be compatible with legacy HTML content while still supporting the changes that this specification introduces to HTML regarding the namespace used for HTML elements&#44; and by the desire to use XPath 1&#46;0 rather than XPath 2&#46;0&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This change is a <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;willful&#45;violation"></a>[willful violation](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#willful-violation) of the XPath 1&#46;0 specification&#44; motivated by desire to have implementations be compatible with legacy content while still supporting the changes that this specification introduces to HTML regarding which namespace is used for HTML elements&#46; [&#91;XPATH10&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXPATH10)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a id="dom&#45;based&#45;xslt&#45;1&#46;0&#45;processors"></a>XSLT 1&#46;0 processors outputting to a DOM when the output method is &#34;html&#34; &#40;either explicitly or via the defaulting rule in XSLT 1&#46;0&#41; are affected as follows&#58;

If the transformation program outputs an element in no namespace&#44; the processor must&#44; prior to constructing the corresponding DOM element node&#44; change the namespace of the element to the <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#44; <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;converted&#45;to&#45;ascii&#45;lowercase"></a>[ASCII&#45;lowercase](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase) the element&#39;s local name&#44; and <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;converted&#45;to&#45;ascii&#45;lowercase&#45;2"></a>[ASCII&#45;lowercase](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lowercase) the names of any non&#45;namespaced attributes on the element&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This requirement is a <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;willful&#45;violation&#45;2"></a>[willful violation](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#willful-violation) of the XSLT 1&#46;0 specification&#44; required because this specification changes the namespaces and case&#45;sensitivity rules of HTML in a manner that would otherwise be incompatible with DOM&#45;based XSLT transformations&#46; &#40;Processors that serialize the output are unaffected&#46;&#41; [&#91;XSLT10&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXSLT10)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

This specification does not specify precisely how XSLT processing interacts with the <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;html&#45;parser"></a>[HTML parser](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#html-parser) infrastructure &#40;for example&#44; whether an XSLT processor acts as if it puts any elements into a <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;stack&#45;of&#45;open&#45;elements"></a>[stack of open elements](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#stack-of-open-elements)&#41;&#46; However&#44; XSLT processors must <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;stop&#45;parsing"></a>[stop parsing](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#stop-parsing) if they successfully complete&#44; and must <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;update&#45;the&#45;current&#45;document&#45;readiness"></a>[update the current document readiness](#update-the-current-document-readiness) first to &#34;<code>interactive</code>&#34; and then to &#34;<code>complete</code>&#34; if they are aborted&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------
