This specification does not specify how XSLT interacts with the <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;navigate"></a>[navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#navigate) algorithm&#44; how it fits in with the <a id="interactions&#45;with&#45;xpath&#45;and&#45;xslt&#58;event&#45;loop"></a>[event loop](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-loop)&#44; nor how error pages are to be handled &#40;e&#46;g&#46; whether XSLT errors are to replace an incremental XSLT output&#44; or are rendered inline&#44; etc&#46;&#41;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

There are also additional non&#45;normative comments regarding the interaction of XSLT and HTML [in the <code>script</code> element section](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#scriptTagXSLT)&#44; and of XSLT&#44; XPath&#44; and HTML [in the <code>template</code> element section](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#template-XSLT-XPath)&#46;

### <a id="common&#45;microsyntaxes"></a>2&#46;3 Common microsyntaxes[](#common-microsyntaxes)

There are various places in HTML that accept particular data types&#44; such as dates or numbers&#46; This section describes what the conformance criteria for content in those formats is&#44; and how to parse them&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Implementers are strongly urged to carefully examine any third&#45;party libraries they might consider using to implement the parsing of syntaxes described below&#46; For example&#44; date libraries are likely to implement error handling behavior that differs from what is required in this specification&#44; since error&#45;handling behavior is often not defined in specifications that describe date syntaxes similar to those used in this specification&#44; and thus implementations tend to vary greatly in how they handle errors&#46;

#### <a id="common&#45;parser&#45;idioms"></a>2&#46;3&#46;1 Common parser idioms[](#common-parser-idioms)

Some of the micro&#45;parsers described below follow the pattern of having an <var>input</var> variable that holds the string being parsed&#44; and having a <var>position</var> variable pointing at the next character to parse in <var>input</var>&#46;

#### <a id="boolean&#45;attributes"></a>2&#46;3&#46;2 Boolean attributes[](#boolean-attributes)

A number of attributes are <a id="boolean&#45;attribute"></a><strong>boolean attributes</strong>&#46; The presence of a boolean attribute on an element represents the true value&#44; and the absence of the attribute represents the false value&#46;

If the attribute is present&#44; its value must either be the empty string or a value that is an <a id="boolean&#45;attributes&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive) match for the attribute&#39;s canonical name&#44; with no leading or trailing whitespace&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The values &#34;true&#34; and &#34;false&#34; are not allowed on boolean attributes&#46; To represent a false value&#44; the attribute has to be omitted altogether&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Here is an example of a checkbox that is checked and disabled&#46; The <a id="boolean&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;checked"></a><code>[checked](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-input-checked)</code> and <a id="boolean&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;disabled"></a><code>[disabled](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fe-disabled)</code> attributes are the boolean attributes&#46;

``` text
<label><input type=checkbox checked name=cheese disabled> Cheese</label>
```

This could be equivalently written as this&#58;

``` text
<label><input type=checkbox checked=checked name=cheese disabled=disabled> Cheese</label>
```

You can also mix styles&#59; the following is still equivalent&#58;

``` text
<label><input type='checkbox' checked name=cheese disabled=""> Cheese</label>
```

#### <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes"></a>2&#46;3&#46;3 Keywords and enumerated attributes[](#keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)

Some attributes&#44; called <a id="enumerated&#45;attribute"></a><strong>enumerated attributes</strong>&#44; take on a finite set of states&#46; The state for such an attribute is derived by combining the attribute&#39;s value&#44; a set of keyword&#47;state mappings&#44; and three possible special states that can also be given in the specification of the attribute&#46; These special states are the <a id="invalid&#45;value&#45;default"></a><strong><em>invalid value default</em></strong>&#44; the <a id="missing&#45;value&#45;default"></a><strong><em>missing value default</em></strong>&#44; and the <a id="empty&#45;value&#45;default"></a><strong><em>empty value default</em></strong>&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Multiple keywords can map to the same state&#46;

To determine the state of an attribute&#44; use the following steps&#58;

1.  If the attribute is not specified&#58;

    1.  If the attribute has a <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;missing&#45;value&#45;default"></a><em>[missing value default](#missing-value-default)</em> state defined&#44; then return that <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;missing&#45;value&#45;default&#45;2"></a><em>[missing value default](#missing-value-default)</em> state&#46;

    2.  Otherwise&#44; return no state&#46;

2.  If the attribute&#39;s value is an <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the keywords defined for the attribute&#44; then return the state represented by that keyword&#46;

3.  If the attribute has an <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;empty&#45;value&#45;default"></a><em>[empty value default](#empty-value-default)</em> state defined and the attribute&#39;s value is the empty string&#44; then return that <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;empty&#45;value&#45;default&#45;2"></a><em>[empty value default](#empty-value-default)</em> state&#46;

4.  If the attribute has an <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;invalid&#45;value&#45;default"></a><em>[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)</em> state defined&#44; then return that <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;invalid&#45;value&#45;default&#45;2"></a><em>[invalid value default](#invalid-value-default)</em> state&#46;

5.  Return no state&#46;

For authoring conformance purposes&#44; if an enumerated attribute is specified&#44; the attribute&#39;s value must be one of&#58;

- An <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive&#45;2"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive) match for one of the conforming keywords for that attribute&#44; with no leading or trailing whitespace&#46;

- The empty string and the attribute must have an <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;empty&#45;value&#45;default&#45;3"></a><em>[empty value default](#empty-value-default)</em> defined&#46;

For <a id="keywords&#45;and&#45;enumerated&#45;attributes&#58;reflect"></a>[reflection](#reflect) purposes&#44; states which have any keywords mapping to them are said to have a <a id="canonical&#45;keyword"></a><strong>canonical keyword</strong>&#46; This is determined as follows&#58;

1.  If there is only one keyword mapping to the given state&#44; then it is that keyword&#46;

2.  If there is only one <em>conforming</em> keyword mapping to the given state&#44; then it is that conforming keyword&#46;

3.  If there are two conforming keywords mapping to the given state&#44; and one is the empty string&#44; then the canonical keyword will be the conforming keyword that is not the empty string&#46;

4.  Otherwise&#44; the canonical keyword for the state will be explicitly given in the specification for the attribute&#46;

#### <a id="numbers"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4 Numbers[](#numbers)

##### <a id="signed&#45;integers"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4&#46;1 Signed integers[](#signed-integers)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;integer"></a><strong>valid integer</strong> if it consists of one or more <a id="signed&#45;integers&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; optionally prefixed with a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;&#46;

A <a id="signed&#45;integers&#58;valid&#45;integer"></a>[valid integer](#valid-integer) without a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS &#40;&#45;&#41; prefix represents the number that is represented in base ten by that string of digits&#46; A <a id="signed&#45;integers&#58;valid&#45;integer&#45;2"></a>[valid integer](#valid-integer) <em>with</em> a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS &#40;&#45;&#41; prefix represents the number represented in base ten by the string of digits that follows the U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS&#44; subtracted from zero&#46;

The <a id="rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;integers"></a><strong>rules for parsing integers</strong> are as given in the following algorithm&#46; When invoked&#44; the steps must be followed in the order given&#44; aborting at the first step that returns a value&#46; This algorithm will return either an integer or an error&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  Let <var>sign</var> have the value &#34;positive&#34;&#46;

4.  <a id="signed&#45;integers&#58;skip&#45;ascii&#45;whitespace"></a>[Skip ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace) within <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46;

5.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; return an error&#46;

6.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> &#40;the first character&#41; is a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;&#58;

    1.  Let <var>sign</var> be &#34;negative&#34;&#46;
    2.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46;
    3.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; return an error&#46;

    Otherwise&#44; if the character indicated by <var>position</var> &#40;the first character&#41; is a U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN character &#40;&#43;&#41;&#58;

    1.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46; &#40;The &#34;<code>&#43;</code>&#34; is ignored&#44; but it is not conforming&#46;&#41;
    2.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; return an error&#46;

7.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is not an <a id="signed&#45;integers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then return an error&#46;

8.  <a id="signed&#45;integers&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="signed&#45;integers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#44; and interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>value</var> be that integer&#46;

9.  If <var>sign</var> is &#34;positive&#34;&#44; return <var>value</var>&#44; otherwise return the result of subtracting <var>value</var> from zero&#46;

##### <a id="non&#45;negative&#45;integers"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4&#46;2 Non&#45;negative integers[](#non-negative-integers)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integer"></a><strong>valid non&#45;negative integer</strong> if it consists of one or more <a id="non&#45;negative&#45;integers&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#46;

A <a id="non&#45;negative&#45;integers&#58;valid&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integer"></a>[valid non&#45;negative integer](#valid-non-negative-integer) represents the number that is represented in base ten by that string of digits&#46;

The <a id="rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integers"></a><strong>rules for parsing non&#45;negative integers</strong> are as given in the following algorithm&#46; When invoked&#44; the steps must be followed in the order given&#44; aborting at the first step that returns a value&#46; This algorithm will return either zero&#44; a positive integer&#44; or an error&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>value</var> be the result of parsing <var>input</var> using the <a id="non&#45;negative&#45;integers&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;integers"></a>[rules for parsing integers](#rules-for-parsing-integers)&#46;

3.  If <var>value</var> is an error&#44; return an error&#46;

4.  If <var>value</var> is less than zero&#44; return an error&#46;

5.  Return <var>value</var>&#46;

##### <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4&#46;3 Floating&#45;point numbers[](#floating-point-numbers)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a><strong>valid floating&#45;point number</strong> if it consists of&#58;

1.  Optionally&#44; a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;&#46;

2.  One or both of the following&#44; in the given order&#58;

    1.  A series of one or more <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#46;

    2.  Both of the following&#44; in the given order&#58;

        1.  A single U&#43;002E FULL STOP character &#40;&#46;&#41;&#46;

        2.  A series of one or more <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#46;

3.  Optionally&#58;

    1.  Either a U&#43;0065 LATIN SMALL LETTER E character &#40;e&#41; or a U&#43;0045 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E character &#40;E&#41;&#46;

    2.  Optionally&#44; a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41; or U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN character &#40;&#43;&#41;&#46;

    3.  A series of one or more <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#46;

A <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a>[valid floating&#45;point number](#valid-floating-point-number) represents the number obtained by multiplying the significand by ten raised to the power of the exponent&#44; where the significand is the first number&#44; interpreted as base ten &#40;including the decimal point and the number after the decimal point&#44; if any&#44; and interpreting the significand as a negative number if the whole string starts with a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41; and the number is not zero&#41;&#44; and where the exponent is the number after the E&#44; if any &#40;interpreted as a negative number if there is a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41; between the E and the number and the number is not zero&#44; or else ignoring a U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN character &#40;&#43;&#41; between the E and the number if there is one&#41;&#46; If there is no E&#44; then the exponent is treated as zero&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The Infinity and Not&#45;a&#45;Number &#40;NaN&#41; values are not <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;2"></a>[valid floating&#45;point numbers](#valid-floating-point-number)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;3"></a>[valid floating&#45;point number](#valid-floating-point-number) concept is typically only used to restrict what is allowed for authors&#44; while the user agent requirements use the <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values"></a>[rules for parsing floating&#45;point number values](#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) below &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; the <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;attr&#45;progress&#45;max"></a><code>[max](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-progress-max)</code> attribute of the <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;the&#45;progress&#45;element"></a><code>[progress](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-progress-element)</code> element&#41;&#46; However&#44; in some cases the user agent requirements include checking if a string is a <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;4"></a>[valid floating&#45;point number](#valid-floating-point-number) &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; the <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;value&#45;sanitization&#45;algorithm"></a>[value sanitization algorithm](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#value-sanitization-algorithm) for the <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;number&#45;state&#45;&#40;type&#61;number&#41;"></a>[Number](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#number-state-(type=number)) state of the <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-input-element)</code> element&#44; or the <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute"></a>[parse a srcset attribute](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#parse-a-srcset-attribute) algorithm&#41;&#46;

The <a id="best&#45;representation&#45;of&#45;the&#45;number&#45;as&#45;a&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a><strong>best representation of the number <var>n</var> as a floating&#45;point number</strong> is the string obtained from running <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;tostring"></a>[ToString](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-tostring)&#40;<var>n</var>&#41;&#46; The abstract operation <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;tostring&#45;2"></a>[ToString](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-tostring) is not uniquely determined&#46; When there are multiple possible strings that could be obtained from <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;tostring&#45;3"></a>[ToString](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-tostring) for a particular value&#44; the user agent must always return the same string for that value &#40;though it may differ from the value used by other user agents&#41;&#46;

The <a id="rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values"></a><strong>rules for parsing floating&#45;point number values</strong> are as given in the following algorithm&#46; This algorithm must be aborted at the first step that returns something&#46; This algorithm will return either a number or an error&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  Let <var>value</var> have the value 1&#46;

4.  Let <var>divisor</var> have the value 1&#46;

5.  Let <var>exponent</var> have the value 1&#46;

6.  <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;skip&#45;ascii&#45;whitespace"></a>[Skip ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace) within <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46;

7.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; return an error&#46;

8.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;&#58;

    1.  Change <var>value</var> and <var>divisor</var> to −1&#46;
    2.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46;
    3.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; return an error&#46;

    Otherwise&#44; if the character indicated by <var>position</var> &#40;the first character&#41; is a U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN character &#40;&#43;&#41;&#58;

    1.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46; &#40;The &#34;<code>&#43;</code>&#34; is ignored&#44; but it is not conforming&#46;&#41;
    2.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; return an error&#46;

9.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is a U&#43;002E FULL STOP &#40;&#46;&#41;&#44; and that is not the last character in <var>input</var>&#44; and the character after the character indicated by <var>position</var> is an <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;4"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then set <var>value</var> to zero and jump to the step labeled <em>fraction</em>&#46;

10. If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is not an <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;5"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then return an error&#46;

11. <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;6"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#44; and interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Multiply <var>value</var> by that integer&#46;

12. If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; jump to the step labeled <em>conversion</em>&#46;

13. <em>Fraction</em>&#58; If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is a U&#43;002E FULL STOP &#40;&#46;&#41;&#44; run these substeps&#58;

    1.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46;

    2.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; or if the character indicated by <var>position</var> is not an <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;7"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; U&#43;0065 LATIN SMALL LETTER E &#40;e&#41;&#44; or U&#43;0045 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E &#40;E&#41;&#44; then jump to the step labeled <em>conversion</em>&#46;

    3.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is a U&#43;0065 LATIN SMALL LETTER E character &#40;e&#41; or a U&#43;0045 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER E character &#40;E&#41;&#44; skip the remainder of these substeps&#46;

    4.  <em>Fraction loop</em>&#58; Multiply <var>divisor</var> by ten&#46;

    5.  Add the value of the character indicated by <var>position</var>&#44; interpreted as a base&#45;ten digit &#40;0&#46;&#46;9&#41; and divided by <var>divisor</var>&#44; to <var>value</var>&#46;

    6.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46;

    7.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then jump to the step labeled <em>conversion</em>&#46;

    8.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is an <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;8"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; jump back to the step labeled <em>fraction loop</em> in these substeps&#46;

14. If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is U&#43;0065 &#40;e&#41; or a U&#43;0045 &#40;E&#41;&#58;

    1.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46;

    2.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then jump to the step labeled <em>conversion</em>&#46;

    3.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;&#58;

        1.  Change <var>exponent</var> to −1&#46;

        2.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46;

        3.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then jump to the step labeled <em>conversion</em>&#46;

        Otherwise&#44; if the character indicated by <var>position</var> is a U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN character &#40;&#43;&#41;&#58;

        1.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character&#46;

        2.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then jump to the step labeled <em>conversion</em>&#46;

    4.  If the character indicated by <var>position</var> is not an <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;9"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then jump to the step labeled <em>conversion</em>&#46;

    5.  <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;10"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#44; and interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Multiply <var>exponent</var> by that integer&#46;

    6.  Multiply <var>value</var> by ten raised to the <var>exponent</var>th power&#46;

15. <em>Conversion</em>&#58; Let <var>S</var> be the set of finite IEEE 754 double&#45;precision floating&#45;point values except −0&#44; but with two special values added&#58; 2<sup>1024</sup> and −2<sup>1024</sup>&#46;

16. Let <var>rounded&#45;value</var> be the number in <var>S</var> that is closest to <var>value</var>&#44; selecting the number with an even significand if there are two equally close values&#46; &#40;The two special values 2<sup>1024</sup> and −2<sup>1024</sup> are considered to have even significands for this purpose&#46;&#41;

17. If <var>rounded&#45;value</var> is 2<sup>1024</sup> or −2<sup>1024</sup>&#44; return an error&#46;

18. Return <var>rounded&#45;value</var>&#46;

##### <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4&#46;4 Percentages and lengths[](#percentages-and-dimensions)

The <a id="rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;dimension&#45;values"></a><strong>rules for parsing dimension values</strong> are as given in the following algorithm&#46; When invoked&#44; the steps must be followed in the order given&#44; aborting at the first step that returns a value&#46; This algorithm will return either a number greater than or equal to 0&#46;0&#44; or failure&#59; if a number is returned&#44; then it is further categorized as either a percentage or a length&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;position&#45;variable"></a>[position variable](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string-position-variable) for <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of <var>input</var>&#46;

3.  <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;skip&#45;ascii&#45;whitespace"></a>[Skip ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace) within <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46;

4.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var> or the code point at <var>position</var> within <var>input</var> is not an <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then return failure&#46;

5.  <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#44; and interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>value</var> be that number&#46;

6.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then return <var>value</var> as a length&#46;

7.  If the code point at <var>position</var> within <var>input</var> is U&#43;002E &#40;&#46;&#41;&#58;

    1.  Advance <var>position</var> by 1&#46;

    2.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var> or the code point at <var>position</var> within <var>input</var> is not an <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then return the <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;current&#45;dimension&#45;value"></a>[current dimension value](#current-dimension-value) with <var>value</var>&#44; <var>input</var>&#44; and <var>position</var>&#46;

    3.  Let <var>divisor</var> have the value 1&#46;

    4.  While true&#58;

        1.  Multiply <var>divisor</var> by ten&#46;

        2.  Add the value of the code point at <var>position</var> within <var>input</var>&#44; interpreted as a base&#45;ten digit &#40;0&#46;&#46;9&#41; and divided by <var>divisor</var>&#44; to <var>value</var>&#46;

        3.  Advance <var>position</var> by 1&#46;

        4.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then return <var>value</var> as a length&#46;

        5.  If the code point at <var>position</var> within <var>input</var> is not an <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;4"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;break"></a>[break](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-break)&#46;

8.  Return the <a id="percentages&#45;and&#45;dimensions&#58;current&#45;dimension&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[current dimension value](#current-dimension-value) with <var>value</var>&#44; <var>input</var>&#44; and <var>position</var>&#46;

The <a id="current&#45;dimension&#45;value"></a><strong>current dimension value</strong>&#44; given <var>value</var>&#44; <var>input</var>&#44; and <var>position</var>&#44; is determined as follows&#58;

1.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then return <var>value</var> as a length&#46;

2.  If the code point at <var>position</var> within <var>input</var> is U&#43;0025 &#40;&#37;&#41;&#44; then return <var>value</var> as a percentage&#46;

3.  Return <var>value</var> as a length&#46;

##### <a id="nonzero&#45;percentages&#45;and&#45;lengths"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4&#46;5 Nonzero percentages and lengths[](#nonzero-percentages-and-lengths)

The <a id="rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;non&#45;zero&#45;dimension&#45;values"></a><strong>rules for parsing nonzero dimension values</strong> are as given in the following algorithm&#46; When invoked&#44; the steps must be followed in the order given&#44; aborting at the first step that returns a value&#46; This algorithm will return either a number greater than 0&#46;0&#44; or an error&#59; if a number is returned&#44; then it is further categorized as either a percentage or a length&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>value</var> be the result of parsing <var>input</var> using the <a id="nonzero&#45;percentages&#45;and&#45;lengths&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;dimension&#45;values"></a>[rules for parsing dimension values](#rules-for-parsing-dimension-values)&#46;

3.  If <var>value</var> is an error&#44; return an error&#46;

4.  If <var>value</var> is zero&#44; return an error&#46;

5.  If <var>value</var> is a percentage&#44; return <var>value</var> as a percentage&#46;

6.  Return <var>value</var> as a length&#46;

##### <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4&#46;6 Lists of floating&#45;point numbers[](#lists-of-floating-point-numbers)

A <a id="valid&#45;list&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers"></a><strong>valid list of floating&#45;point numbers</strong> is a number of <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a>[valid floating&#45;point numbers](#valid-floating-point-number) separated by U&#43;002C COMMA characters&#44; with no other characters &#40;e&#46;g&#46; no <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;space&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#41;&#46; In addition&#44; there might be restrictions on the number of floating&#45;point numbers that can be given&#44; or on the range of values allowed&#46;

The <a id="rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;a&#45;list&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers"></a><strong>rules for parsing a list of floating&#45;point numbers</strong> are as follows&#58;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  Let <var>numbers</var> be an initially empty list of floating&#45;point numbers&#46; This list will be the result of this algorithm&#46;

4.  <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;2"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#44; U&#43;002C COMMA&#44; or U&#43;003B SEMICOLON characters from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; This skips past any leading delimiters&#46;

5.  While <var>position</var> is not past the end of <var>input</var>&#58;

    1.  <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are not <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;3"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#44; U&#43;002C COMMA&#44; U&#43;003B SEMICOLON&#44; <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; U&#43;002E FULL STOP&#44; or U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS characters from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; This skips past leading garbage&#46;

    2.  <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;3"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are not <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;4"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#44; U&#43;002C COMMA&#44; or U&#43;003B SEMICOLON characters from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#44; and let <var>unparsed number</var> be the result&#46;

    3.  Let <var>number</var> be the result of parsing <var>unparsed number</var> using the <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values"></a>[rules for parsing floating&#45;point number values](#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values)&#46;

    4.  If <var>number</var> is an error&#44; set <var>number</var> to zero&#46;

    5.  Append <var>number</var> to <var>numbers</var>&#46;

    6.  <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;4"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;numbers&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;5"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#44; U&#43;002C COMMA&#44; or U&#43;003B SEMICOLON characters from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; This skips past the delimiter&#46;

6.  Return <var>numbers</var>&#46;

##### <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions"></a>2&#46;3&#46;4&#46;7 Lists of dimensions[](#lists-of-dimensions)

The <a id="rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;a&#45;list&#45;of&#45;dimensions"></a><strong>rules for parsing a list of dimensions</strong> are as follows&#46; These rules return a list of zero or more pairs consisting of a number and a unit&#44; the unit being one of <em>percentage</em>&#44; <em>relative</em>&#44; and <em>absolute</em>&#46;

1.  Let <var>raw input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  If the last character in <var>raw input</var> is a U&#43;002C COMMA character &#40;&#44;&#41;&#44; then remove that character from <var>raw input</var>&#46;

3.  <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;split&#45;a&#45;string&#45;on&#45;commas"></a>[Split the string <var>raw input</var> on commas](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#split-on-commas)&#46; Let <var>raw tokens</var> be the resulting list of tokens&#46;

4.  Let <var>result</var> be an empty list of number&#47;unit pairs&#46;

5.  For each token in <var>raw tokens</var>&#44; run the following substeps&#58;

    1.  Let <var>input</var> be the token&#46;

    2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

    3.  Let <var>value</var> be the number 0&#46;

    4.  Let <var>unit</var> be <em>absolute</em>&#46;

    5.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; set <var>unit</var> to <em>relative</em> and jump to the last substep&#46;

    6.  If the character at <var>position</var> is an <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digit](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as an integer in base ten&#44; and increment <var>value</var> by that integer&#46;

    7.  If the character at <var>position</var> is U&#43;002E &#40;&#46;&#41;&#58;

        1.  <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) consisting of <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;space&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace) and <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; Let <var>s</var> be the resulting sequence&#46;

        2.  Remove all <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;2"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace) in <var>s</var>&#46;

        3.  If <var>s</var> is not the empty string&#58;

            1.  Let <var>length</var> be the number of characters in <var>s</var> &#40;after the spaces were removed&#41;&#46;

            2.  Let <var>fraction</var> be the result of interpreting <var>s</var> as a base&#45;ten integer&#44; and then dividing that number by 10<sup><var>length</var></sup>&#46;

            3.  Increment <var>value</var> by <var>fraction</var>&#46;

    8.  <a id="lists&#45;of&#45;dimensions&#58;skip&#45;ascii&#45;whitespace"></a>[Skip ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace) within <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46;

    9.  If the character at <var>position</var> is a U&#43;0025 PERCENT SIGN character &#40;&#37;&#41;&#44; then set <var>unit</var> to <em>percentage</em>&#46;

        Otherwise&#44; if the character at <var>position</var> is a U&#43;002A ASTERISK character &#40;&#42;&#41;&#44; then set <var>unit</var> to <em>relative</em>&#46;

    10. Add an entry to <var>result</var> consisting of the number given by <var>value</var> and the unit given by <var>unit</var>&#46;

6.  Return the list <var>result</var>&#46;

#### <a id="dates&#45;and&#45;times"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5 Dates and times[](#dates-and-times)

In the algorithms below&#44; the <a id="number&#45;of&#45;days&#45;in&#45;month&#45;month&#45;of&#45;year&#45;year"></a><strong>number of days in month <var>month</var> of year <var>year</var></strong> is&#58; <em>31</em> if <var>month</var> is 1&#44; 3&#44; 5&#44; 7&#44; 8&#44; 10&#44; or 12&#59; <em>30</em> if <var>month</var> is 4&#44; 6&#44; 9&#44; or 11&#59; <em>29</em> if <var>month</var> is 2 and <var>year</var> is a number divisible by 400&#44; or if <var>year</var> is a number divisible by 4 but not by 100&#59; and <em>28</em> otherwise&#46; This takes into account leap years in the Gregorian calendar&#46; [&#91;GREGORIAN&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsGREGORIAN)

When <a id="dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) are used in the date and time syntaxes defined in this section&#44; they express numbers in base ten&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

While the formats described here are intended to be subsets of the corresponding ISO8601 formats&#44; this specification defines parsing rules in much more detail than ISO8601&#46; Implementers are therefore encouraged to carefully examine any date parsing libraries before using them to implement the parsing rules described below&#59; ISO8601 libraries might not parse dates and times in exactly the same manner&#46; [&#91;ISO8601&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsISO8601)

Where this specification refers to the <a id="proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;calendar"></a><strong>proleptic Gregorian calendar</strong>&#44; it means the modern Gregorian calendar&#44; extrapolated backwards to year 1&#46; A date in the <a id="dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;calendar"></a>[proleptic Gregorian calendar](#proleptic-gregorian-calendar)&#44; sometimes explicitly referred to as a <a id="proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;date"></a><strong>proleptic&#45;Gregorian date</strong>&#44; is one that is described using that calendar even if that calendar was not in use at the time &#40;or place&#41; in question&#46; [&#91;GREGORIAN&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsGREGORIAN)

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The use of the Gregorian calendar as the wire format in this specification is an arbitrary choice resulting from the cultural biases of those involved in the decision&#46; See also the section discussing [date&#44; time&#44; and number formats](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#input-author-notes) in forms &#40;for authors&#41;&#44; [implementation notes regarding localization of form controls](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#input-impl-notes)&#44; and the <a id="dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;the&#45;time&#45;element"></a><code>[time](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-time-element)</code> element&#46;

##### <a id="months"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5&#46;1 Months[](#months)

A <a id="concept&#45;month"></a><strong>month</strong> consists of a specific <a id="months&#58;proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;date"></a>[proleptic&#45;Gregorian date](#proleptic-gregorian-date) with no time&#45;zone information and no date information beyond a year and a month&#46; [&#91;GREGORIAN&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsGREGORIAN)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;month&#45;string"></a><strong>valid month string</strong> representing a year <var>year</var> and month <var>month</var> if it consists of the following components in the given order&#58;

1.  Four or more <a id="months&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing <var>year</var>&#44; where <var>year</var> &#62; 0
2.  A U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;
3.  Two <a id="months&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing the month <var>month</var>&#44; in the range 1 ≤ <var>month</var> ≤ 12

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;month&#45;string"></a><strong>parse a month string</strong> are as follows&#46; This will return either a year and month&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  <a id="months&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;month&#45;component"></a>[Parse a month component](#parse-a-month-component) to obtain <var>year</var> and <var>month</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

4.  If <var>position</var> is <em>not</em> beyond the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

5.  Return <var>year</var> and <var>month</var>&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;month&#45;component"></a><strong>parse a month component</strong>&#44; given an <var>input</var> string and a <var>position</var>&#44; are as follows&#46; This will return either a year and a month&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  <a id="months&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="months&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not at least four characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>year</var> be that number&#46;

2.  If <var>year</var> is not a number greater than zero&#44; then fail&#46;

3.  If <var>position</var> is beyond the end of <var>input</var> or if the character at <var>position</var> is not a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; move <var>position</var> forwards one character&#46;

4.  <a id="months&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="months&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;4"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>month</var> be that number&#46;

5.  If <var>month</var> is not a number in the range 1 ≤ <var>month</var> ≤ 12&#44; then fail&#46;

6.  Return <var>year</var> and <var>month</var>&#46;

##### <a id="dates"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5&#46;2 Dates[](#dates)

A <a id="concept&#45;date"></a><strong>date</strong> consists of a specific <a id="dates&#58;proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;date"></a>[proleptic&#45;Gregorian date](#proleptic-gregorian-date) with no time&#45;zone information&#44; consisting of a year&#44; a month&#44; and a day&#46; [&#91;GREGORIAN&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsGREGORIAN)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;date&#45;string"></a><strong>valid date string</strong> representing a year <var>year</var>&#44; month <var>month</var>&#44; and day <var>day</var> if it consists of the following components in the given order&#58;

1.  A <a id="dates&#58;valid&#45;month&#45;string"></a>[valid month string](#valid-month-string)&#44; representing <var>year</var> and <var>month</var>
2.  A U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;
3.  Two <a id="dates&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing <var>day</var>&#44; in the range 1 ≤ <var>day</var> ≤ <var>maxday</var> where <var>maxday</var> is the <a id="dates&#58;number&#45;of&#45;days&#45;in&#45;month&#45;month&#45;of&#45;year&#45;year"></a>[number of days in the month <var>month</var> and year <var>year</var>](#number-of-days-in-month-month-of-year-year)

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;date&#45;string"></a><strong>parse a date string</strong> are as follows&#46; This will return either a date&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  <a id="dates&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;date&#45;component"></a>[Parse a date component](#parse-a-date-component) to obtain <var>year</var>&#44; <var>month</var>&#44; and <var>day</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

4.  If <var>position</var> is <em>not</em> beyond the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

5.  Let <var>date</var> be the date with year <var>year</var>&#44; month <var>month</var>&#44; and day <var>day</var>&#46;

6.  Return <var>date</var>&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;date&#45;component"></a><strong>parse a date component</strong>&#44; given an <var>input</var> string and a <var>position</var>&#44; are as follows&#46; This will return either a year&#44; a month&#44; and a day&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  <a id="dates&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;month&#45;component"></a>[Parse a month component](#parse-a-month-component) to obtain <var>year</var> and <var>month</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

2.  Let <var>maxday</var> be the <a id="dates&#58;number&#45;of&#45;days&#45;in&#45;month&#45;month&#45;of&#45;year&#45;year&#45;2"></a>[number of days in month <var>month</var> of year <var>year</var>](#number-of-days-in-month-month-of-year-year)&#46;

3.  If <var>position</var> is beyond the end of <var>input</var> or if the character at <var>position</var> is not a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; move <var>position</var> forwards one character&#46;

4.  <a id="dates&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="dates&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>day</var> be that number&#46;

5.  If <var>day</var> is not a number in the range 1 ≤ <var>day</var> ≤ <var>maxday</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

6.  Return <var>year</var>&#44; <var>month</var>&#44; and <var>day</var>&#46;

##### <a id="yearless&#45;dates"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5&#46;3 Yearless dates[](#yearless-dates)

A <a id="concept&#45;yearless&#45;date"></a><strong>yearless date</strong> consists of a Gregorian month and a day within that month&#44; but with no associated year&#46; [&#91;GREGORIAN&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsGREGORIAN)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;yearless&#45;date&#45;string"></a><strong>valid yearless date string</strong> representing a month <var>month</var> and a day <var>day</var> if it consists of the following components in the given order&#58;

1.  Optionally&#44; two U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS characters &#40;&#45;&#41;
2.  Two <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing the month <var>month</var>&#44; in the range 1 ≤ <var>month</var> ≤ 12
3.  A U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;
4.  Two <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing <var>day</var>&#44; in the range 1 ≤ <var>day</var> ≤ <var>maxday</var> where <var>maxday</var> is the <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;number&#45;of&#45;days&#45;in&#45;month&#45;month&#45;of&#45;year&#45;year"></a>[number of days](#number-of-days-in-month-month-of-year-year) in the month <var>month</var> and any arbitrary leap year &#40;e&#46;g&#46; 4 or 2000&#41;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

In other words&#44; if the <var>month</var> is &#34;<code>02</code>&#34;&#44; meaning February&#44; then the day can be 29&#44; as if the year was a leap year&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;yearless&#45;date&#45;string"></a><strong>parse a yearless date string</strong> are as follows&#46; This will return either a month and a day&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;yearless&#45;date&#45;component"></a>[Parse a yearless date component](#parse-a-yearless-date-component) to obtain <var>month</var> and <var>day</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

4.  If <var>position</var> is <em>not</em> beyond the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

5.  Return <var>month</var> and <var>day</var>&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;yearless&#45;date&#45;component"></a><strong>parse a yearless date component</strong>&#44; given an <var>input</var> string and a <var>position</var>&#44; are as follows&#46; This will return either a month and a day&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS characters &#40;&#45;&#41; from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly zero or two characters long&#44; then fail&#46;

2.  <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>month</var> be that number&#46;

3.  If <var>month</var> is not a number in the range 1 ≤ <var>month</var> ≤ 12&#44; then fail&#46;

4.  Let <var>maxday</var> be the <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;number&#45;of&#45;days&#45;in&#45;month&#45;month&#45;of&#45;year&#45;year&#45;2"></a>[number of days](#number-of-days-in-month-month-of-year-year) in month <var>month</var> of any arbitrary leap year &#40;e&#46;g&#46; 4 or 2000&#41;&#46;

5.  If <var>position</var> is beyond the end of <var>input</var> or if the character at <var>position</var> is not a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; move <var>position</var> forwards one character&#46;

6.  <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;3"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="yearless&#45;dates&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;4"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>day</var> be that number&#46;

7.  If <var>day</var> is not a number in the range 1 ≤ <var>day</var> ≤ <var>maxday</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

8.  Return <var>month</var> and <var>day</var>&#46;

##### <a id="times"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5&#46;4 Times[](#times)

A <a id="concept&#45;time"></a><strong>time</strong> consists of a specific time with no time&#45;zone information&#44; consisting of an hour&#44; a minute&#44; a second&#44; and a fraction of a second&#46;

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;time&#45;string"></a><strong>valid time string</strong> representing an hour <var>hour</var>&#44; a minute <var>minute</var>&#44; and a second <var>second</var> if it consists of the following components in the given order&#58;

1.  Two <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing <var>hour</var>&#44; in the range 0 ≤ <var>hour</var> ≤ 23
2.  A U&#43;003A COLON character &#40;&#58;&#41;
3.  Two <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing <var>minute</var>&#44; in the range 0 ≤ <var>minute</var> ≤ 59
4.  If <var>second</var> is nonzero&#44; or optionally if <var>second</var> is zero&#58;
    1.  A U&#43;003A COLON character &#40;&#58;&#41;
    2.  Two <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing the integer part of <var>second</var>&#44; in the range 0 ≤ <var>s</var> ≤ 59
    3.  If <var>second</var> is not an integer&#44; or optionally if <var>second</var> is an integer&#58;
        1.  A U&#43;002E FULL STOP character &#40;&#46;&#41;
        2.  One&#44; two&#44; or three <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;4"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing the fractional part of <var>second</var>

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The <var>second</var> component cannot be 60 or 61&#59; leap seconds cannot be represented&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;time&#45;string"></a><strong>parse a time string</strong> are as follows&#46; This will return either a time&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  <a id="times&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;time&#45;component"></a>[Parse a time component](#parse-a-time-component) to obtain <var>hour</var>&#44; <var>minute</var>&#44; and <var>second</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

4.  If <var>position</var> is <em>not</em> beyond the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

5.  Let <var>time</var> be the time with hour <var>hour</var>&#44; minute <var>minute</var>&#44; and second <var>second</var>&#46;

6.  Return <var>time</var>&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;time&#45;component"></a><strong>parse a time component</strong>&#44; given an <var>input</var> string and a <var>position</var>&#44; are as follows&#46; This will return either an hour&#44; a minute&#44; and a second&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  <a id="times&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;5"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>hour</var> be that number&#46;

2.  If <var>hour</var> is not a number in the range 0 ≤ <var>hour</var> ≤ 23&#44; then fail&#46;

3.  If <var>position</var> is beyond the end of <var>input</var> or if the character at <var>position</var> is not a U&#43;003A COLON character&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; move <var>position</var> forwards one character&#46;

4.  <a id="times&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;6"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>minute</var> be that number&#46;

5.  If <var>minute</var> is not a number in the range 0 ≤ <var>minute</var> ≤ 59&#44; then fail&#46;

6.  Let <var>second</var> be 0&#46;

7.  If <var>position</var> is not beyond the end of <var>input</var> and the character at <var>position</var> is U&#43;003A &#40;&#58;&#41;&#58;

    1.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character in <var>input</var>&#46;

    2.  If <var>position</var> is beyond the end of <var>input</var>&#44; or at the last character in <var>input</var>&#44; or if the next <em>two</em> characters in <var>input</var> starting at <var>position</var> are not both <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;7"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; then fail&#46;

    3.  <a id="times&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;3"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are either <a id="times&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;8"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) or U&#43;002E FULL STOP characters from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is three characters long&#44; or if it is longer than three characters long and the third character is not a U&#43;002E FULL STOP character&#44; or if it has more than one U&#43;002E FULL STOP character&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten number &#40;possibly with a fractional part&#41;&#46; Set <var>second</var> to that number&#46;

    4.  If <var>second</var> is not a number in the range 0 ≤ <var>second</var> &#60; 60&#44; then fail&#46;

8.  Return <var>hour</var>&#44; <var>minute</var>&#44; and <var>second</var>&#46;

##### <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5&#46;5 Local dates and times[](#local-dates-and-times)

A <a id="concept&#45;datetime&#45;local"></a><strong>local date and time</strong> consists of a specific <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;date"></a>[proleptic&#45;Gregorian date](#proleptic-gregorian-date)&#44; consisting of a year&#44; a month&#44; and a day&#44; and a time&#44; consisting of an hour&#44; a minute&#44; a second&#44; and a fraction of a second&#44; but expressed without a time zone&#46; [&#91;GREGORIAN&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsGREGORIAN)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;local&#45;date&#45;and&#45;time&#45;string"></a><strong>valid local date and time string</strong> representing a date and time if it consists of the following components in the given order&#58;

1.  A <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;date&#45;string"></a>[valid date string](#valid-date-string) representing the date
2.  A U&#43;0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character &#40;T&#41; or a U&#43;0020 SPACE character
3.  A <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;time&#45;string"></a>[valid time string](#valid-time-string) representing the time

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;normalised&#45;local&#45;date&#45;and&#45;time&#45;string"></a><strong>valid normalized local date and time string</strong> representing a date and time if it consists of the following components in the given order&#58;

1.  A <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;date&#45;string&#45;2"></a>[valid date string](#valid-date-string) representing the date
2.  A U&#43;0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character &#40;T&#41;
3.  A <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;time&#45;string&#45;2"></a>[valid time string](#valid-time-string) representing the time&#44; expressed as the shortest possible string for the given time &#40;e&#46;g&#46; omitting the seconds component entirely if the given time is zero seconds past the minute&#41;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;local&#45;date&#45;and&#45;time&#45;string"></a><strong>parse a local date and time string</strong> are as follows&#46; This will return either a date and time&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;date&#45;component"></a>[Parse a date component](#parse-a-date-component) to obtain <var>year</var>&#44; <var>month</var>&#44; and <var>day</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

4.  If <var>position</var> is beyond the end of <var>input</var> or if the character at <var>position</var> is neither a U&#43;0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character &#40;T&#41; nor a U&#43;0020 SPACE character&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; move <var>position</var> forwards one character&#46;

5.  <a id="local&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;time&#45;component"></a>[Parse a time component](#parse-a-time-component) to obtain <var>hour</var>&#44; <var>minute</var>&#44; and <var>second</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

6.  If <var>position</var> is <em>not</em> beyond the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

7.  Let <var>date</var> be the date with year <var>year</var>&#44; month <var>month</var>&#44; and day <var>day</var>&#46;

8.  Let <var>time</var> be the time with hour <var>hour</var>&#44; minute <var>minute</var>&#44; and second <var>second</var>&#46;

9.  Return <var>date</var> and <var>time</var>&#46;

##### <a id="time&#45;zones"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5&#46;6 Time zones[](#time-zones)

A <a id="concept&#45;timezone"></a><strong>time&#45;zone offset</strong> consists of a signed number of hours and minutes&#46;

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;time&#45;zone&#45;offset&#45;string"></a><strong>valid time&#45;zone offset string</strong> representing a time&#45;zone offset if it consists of either&#58;

- A U&#43;005A LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z character &#40;Z&#41;&#44; allowed only if the time zone is UTC

- Or&#44; the following components&#44; in the given order&#58;

  1.  Either a U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN character &#40;&#43;&#41; or&#44; if the time&#45;zone offset is not zero&#44; a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS character &#40;&#45;&#41;&#44; representing the sign of the time&#45;zone offset
  2.  Two <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing the hours component <var>hour</var> of the time&#45;zone offset&#44; in the range 0 ≤ <var>hour</var> ≤ 23
  3.  Optionally&#44; a U&#43;003A COLON character &#40;&#58;&#41;
  4.  Two <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;2"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing the minutes component <var>minute</var> of the time&#45;zone offset&#44; in the range 0 ≤ <var>minute</var> ≤ 59

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This format allows for time&#45;zone offsets from &#45;23&#58;59 to &#43;23&#58;59&#46; Right now&#44; in practice&#44; the range of offsets of actual time zones is &#45;12&#58;00 to &#43;14&#58;00&#44; and the minutes component of offsets of actual time zones is always either 00&#44; 30&#44; or 45&#46; There is no guarantee that this will remain so forever&#44; however&#44; since time zones are used as political footballs and are thus subject to very whimsical policy decisions&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

See also the usage notes and examples in the <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;concept&#45;datetime"></a>[global date and time](#concept-datetime) section below for details on using time&#45;zone offsets with historical times that predate the formation of formal time zones&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;time&#45;zone&#45;offset&#45;string"></a><strong>parse a time&#45;zone offset string</strong> are as follows&#46; This will return either a time&#45;zone offset&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;time&#45;zone&#45;offset&#45;component"></a>[Parse a time&#45;zone offset component](#parse-a-time-zone-offset-component) to obtain <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> and <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;

4.  If <var>position</var> is <em>not</em> beyond the end of <var>input</var>&#44; then fail&#46;

5.  Return the time&#45;zone offset that is <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> hours and <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var> minutes from UTC&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;time&#45;zone&#45;offset&#45;component"></a><strong>parse a time&#45;zone offset component</strong>&#44; given an <var>input</var> string and a <var>position</var>&#44; are as follows&#46; This will return either time&#45;zone hours and time&#45;zone minutes&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  If the character at <var>position</var> is a U&#43;005A LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z character &#40;Z&#41;&#58;

    1.  Let <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> be 0&#46;

    2.  Let <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var> be 0&#46;

    3.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character in <var>input</var>&#46;

    Otherwise&#44; if the character at <var>position</var> is either a U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN &#40;&#43;&#41; or a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS &#40;&#45;&#41;&#58;

    1.  If the character at <var>position</var> is a U&#43;002B PLUS SIGN &#40;&#43;&#41;&#44; let <var>sign</var> be &#34;positive&#34;&#46; Otherwise&#44; it&#39;s a U&#43;002D HYPHEN&#45;MINUS &#40;&#45;&#41;&#59; let <var>sign</var> be &#34;negative&#34;&#46;

    2.  Advance <var>position</var> to the next character in <var>input</var>&#46;

    3.  <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;3"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; Let <var>s</var> be the collected sequence&#46;

    4.  If <var>s</var> is exactly two characters long&#58;

        1.  Interpret <var>s</var> as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> be that number&#46;

        2.  If <var>position</var> is beyond the end of <var>input</var> or if the character at <var>position</var> is not a U&#43;003A COLON character&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; move <var>position</var> forwards one character&#46;

        3.  <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="time&#45;zones&#58;ascii&#45;digits&#45;4"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If the collected sequence is not exactly two characters long&#44; then fail&#46; Otherwise&#44; interpret the resulting sequence as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var> be that number&#46;

        If <var>s</var> is exactly four characters long&#58;

        1.  Interpret the first two characters of <var>s</var> as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> be that number&#46;

        2.  Interpret the last two characters of <var>s</var> as a base&#45;ten integer&#46; Let <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var> be that number&#46;

        Otherwise&#44; fail&#46;

    5.  If <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> is not a number in the range 0 ≤ <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> ≤ 23&#44; then fail&#46;

    6.  If <var>sign</var> is &#34;negative&#34;&#44; then negate <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var>&#46;

    7.  If <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var> is not a number in the range 0 ≤ <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var> ≤ 59&#44; then fail&#46;

    8.  If <var>sign</var> is &#34;negative&#34;&#44; then negate <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var>&#46;

    Otherwise&#44; fail&#46;

2.  Return <var>timezone<sub>hours</sub></var> and <var>timezone<sub>minutes</sub></var>&#46;

##### <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times"></a>2&#46;3&#46;5&#46;7 Global dates and times[](#global-dates-and-times)

A <a id="concept&#45;datetime"></a><strong>global date and time</strong> consists of a specific <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;date"></a>[proleptic&#45;Gregorian date](#proleptic-gregorian-date)&#44; consisting of a year&#44; a month&#44; and a day&#44; and a time&#44; consisting of an hour&#44; a minute&#44; a second&#44; and a fraction of a second&#44; expressed with a time&#45;zone offset&#44; consisting of a signed number of hours and minutes&#46; [&#91;GREGORIAN&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsGREGORIAN)

A string is a <a id="valid&#45;global&#45;date&#45;and&#45;time&#45;string"></a><strong>valid global date and time string</strong> representing a date&#44; time&#44; and a time&#45;zone offset if it consists of the following components in the given order&#58;

1.  A <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;date&#45;string"></a>[valid date string](#valid-date-string) representing the date
2.  A U&#43;0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character &#40;T&#41; or a U&#43;0020 SPACE character
3.  A <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;time&#45;string"></a>[valid time string](#valid-time-string) representing the time
4.  A <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;time&#45;zone&#45;offset&#45;string"></a>[valid time&#45;zone offset string](#valid-time-zone-offset-string) representing the time&#45;zone offset

Times in dates before the formation of UTC in the mid&#45;twentieth century must be expressed and interpreted in terms of UT1 &#40;contemporary Earth solar time at the 0° longitude&#41;&#44; not UTC &#40;the approximation of UT1 that ticks in SI seconds&#41;&#46; Time before the formation of time zones must be expressed and interpreted as UT1 times with explicit time zones that approximate the contemporary difference between the appropriate local time and the time observed at the location of Greenwich&#44; London&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following are some examples of dates written as <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;valid&#45;global&#45;date&#45;and&#45;time&#45;string"></a>[valid global date and time strings](#valid-global-date-and-time-string)&#46;

<strong>&#34;<code>0037&#45;12&#45;13 00&#58;00Z</code>&#34;</strong>

Midnight in areas using London time on the birthday of Nero &#40;the Roman Emperor&#41;&#46; See below for further discussion on which date this actually corresponds to&#46;

<strong>&#34;<code>1979&#45;10&#45;14T12&#58;00&#58;00&#46;001&#45;04&#58;00</code>&#34;</strong>

One millisecond after noon on October 14th 1979&#44; in the time zone in use on the east coast of the USA during daylight saving time&#46;

<strong>&#34;<code>8592&#45;01&#45;01T02&#58;09&#43;02&#58;09</code>&#34;</strong>

Midnight UTC on the 1st of January&#44; 8592&#46; The time zone associated with that time is two hours and nine minutes ahead of UTC&#44; which is not currently a real time zone&#44; but is nonetheless allowed&#46;

Several things are notable about these dates&#58;

- Years with fewer than four digits have to be zero&#45;padded&#46; The date &#34;37&#45;12&#45;13&#34; would not be a valid date&#46;
- If the &#34;<code>T</code>&#34; is replaced by a space&#44; it must be a single space character&#46; The string &#34;<code>2001&#45;12&#45;21  12&#58;00Z</code>&#34; &#40;with two spaces between the components&#41; would not be parsed successfully&#46;
- To unambiguously identify a moment in time prior to the introduction of the Gregorian calendar &#40;insofar as moments in time before the formation of UTC can be unambiguously identified&#41;&#44; the date has to be first converted to the Gregorian calendar from the calendar in use at the time &#40;e&#46;g&#46; from the Julian calendar&#41;&#46; The date of Nero&#39;s birth is the 15th of December 37&#44; in the Julian Calendar&#44; which is the 13th of December 37 in the <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;proleptic&#45;gregorian&#45;calendar"></a>[proleptic Gregorian calendar](#proleptic-gregorian-calendar)&#46;
- The time and time&#45;zone offset components are not optional&#46;
- Dates before the year one can&#39;t be represented as a datetime in this version of HTML&#46;
- Times of specific events in ancient times are&#44; at best&#44; approximations&#44; since time was not well coordinated or measured until relatively recent decades&#46;
- Time&#45;zone offsets differ based on daylight saving time&#46;

The rules to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;global&#45;date&#45;and&#45;time&#45;string"></a><strong>parse a global date and time string</strong> are as follows&#46; This will return either a time in UTC&#44; with associated time&#45;zone offset information for roundtripping or display purposes&#44; or nothing&#46; If at any point the algorithm says that it &#34;fails&#34;&#44; this means that it is aborted at that point and returns nothing&#46;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the string being parsed&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  <a id="global&#45;dates&#45;and&#45;times&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;date&#45;component"></a>[Parse a date component](#parse-a-date-component) to obtain <var>year</var>&#44; <var>month</var>&#44; and <var>day</var>&#46; If this returns nothing&#44; then fail&#46;
