Returns the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> element&#44; or the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;svg&#45;script"></a>[SVG <code>script</code>](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element&#44; that is currently executing&#44; as long as the element represents a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;classic&#45;script"></a>[classic script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#classic-script)&#46; In the case of reentrant script execution&#44; returns the one that most recently started executing amongst those that have not yet finished executing&#46;

Returns null if the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;13"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> is not currently executing a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> or <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;svg&#45;script&#45;2"></a>[SVG <code>script</code>](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; because the running script is an event handler&#44; or a timeout&#41;&#44; or if the currently executing <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> or <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;svg&#45;script&#45;3"></a>[SVG <code>script</code>](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element represents a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;module&#45;script"></a>[module script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#module-script)&#46;

The <a id="dom&#45;document&#45;currentscript"></a><strong><code>currentScript</code></strong> attribute&#44; on getting&#44; must return the value to which it was most recently set&#46; When the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;14"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> is created&#44; the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;currentscript"></a><code>[currentScript](#dom-document-currentscript)</code> must be initialized to null&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This API has fallen out of favor in the implementer and standards community&#44; as it globally exposes <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> or <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;svg&#45;script&#45;4"></a>[SVG <code>script</code>](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) elements&#46; As such&#44; it is not available in newer contexts&#44; such as when running <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;module&#45;script&#45;2"></a>[module scripts](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#module-script) or when running scripts in a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;shadow&#45;tree"></a>[shadow tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-tree)&#46; We are looking into creating a new solution for identifying the running script in such contexts&#44; which does not make it globally available&#58; see [issue &#35;1013](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1013)&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a id="dom&#45;document&#45;namedItem&#45;which"></a>The <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;15"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> interface <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;support&#45;named&#45;properties"></a>[supports named properties](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-support-named-properties)&#46; The <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;supported&#45;property&#45;names"></a>[supported property names](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-names) of a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;16"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> object <var>document</var> at any moment consist of the following&#44; for each element <var>element</var> <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;in&#45;a&#45;document&#45;tree"></a>[in a document tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree) with <var>document</var> as its <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;root"></a>[root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root)&#44; in <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;tree&#45;order&#45;3"></a>[tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order)&#44; ignoring later duplicates&#58;

- the value of <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;id&#45;attribute"></a><code>[id](#the-id-attribute)</code> content attribute&#44; if <var>element</var> is a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;nameditem&#45;filter"></a>[named element](#dom-document-nameditem-filter) with that value as its name&#59; and then

- the value of <var>element</var>&#39;s <code>name</code> content attribute&#44; if <var>element</var> is a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;nameditem&#45;filter&#45;2"></a>[named element](#dom-document-nameditem-filter) with that value as its name&#46;

<a id="dom&#45;document&#45;nameditem"></a>To <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;determine&#45;the&#45;value&#45;of&#45;a&#45;named&#45;property"></a>[determine the value of a named property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-a-named-property) <var>name</var> for a <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;17"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code>&#44; the user agent must return the value obtained using the following steps&#58;

1.  Let <var>elements</var> be the list of <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;nameditem&#45;filter&#45;3"></a>[named elements](#dom-document-nameditem-filter) with the name <var>name</var> that are <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;in&#45;a&#45;document&#45;tree&#45;2"></a>[in a document tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#in-a-document-tree) with the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;18"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> as their <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;root&#45;2"></a>[root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root)&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    There will be at least one such element&#44; since the algorithm would otherwise not have been <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;legacyplatformobjectgetownproperty"></a>[invoked by Web IDL](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#LegacyPlatformObjectGetOwnProperty)&#46;

2.  If <var>elements</var> has only one element&#44; and that element is an <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;iframe&#45;element"></a><code>[iframe](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-iframe-element)</code> element&#44; and that <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;iframe&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[iframe](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-iframe-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;content&#45;navigable"></a>[content navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#content-navigable) is not null&#44; then return the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;nav&#45;wp"></a>[active <code>WindowProxy</code>](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#nav-wp) of the element&#39;s <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;content&#45;navigable&#45;2"></a>[content navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#content-navigable)&#46;

3.  Otherwise&#44; if <var>elements</var> has only one element&#44; return that element&#46;

4.  Otherwise&#44; return an <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;htmlcollection&#45;11"></a><code>[HTMLCollection](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-htmlcollection)</code> rooted at the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;19"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> node&#44; whose filter matches only <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;nameditem&#45;filter&#45;4"></a>[named elements](#dom-document-nameditem-filter) with the name <var>name</var>&#46;

An element is a <a id="dom&#45;document&#45;nameditem&#45;filter"></a><strong>named element</strong> with the name <var>name</var> if <var>name</var> is not the empty string and any of the following are true&#58;

- it is an <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;embed&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[embed](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-embed-element)</code>&#44; <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[form](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-form-element)</code>&#44; <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;iframe&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[iframe](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-iframe-element)</code>&#44; <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[img](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-img-element)</code>&#44; or <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;object&#45;element"></a><code>[object](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-object-element)</code> element whose <code>name</code> content attribute&#39;s value is <var>name</var>&#59;
- it is an <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;object&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[object](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-object-element)</code> element whose <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;id&#45;attribute&#45;2"></a><code>[id](#the-id-attribute)</code> content attribute&#39;s value is <var>name</var>&#59; or
- it is an <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[img](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-img-element)</code> element whose <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;the&#45;id&#45;attribute&#45;3"></a><code>[id](#the-id-attribute)</code> content attribute&#39;s value is <var>name</var>&#44; and that has a non&#45;empty <code>name</code> content attribute present also&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;dir"></a><code>[dir](#dom-document-dir)</code> attribute on the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;document&#45;20"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> interface is defined along with the <a id="dom&#45;tree&#45;accessors&#58;attr&#45;dir"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> content attribute&#46;

### <a id="elements"></a>3&#46;2 Elements[](#elements)

#### <a id="semantics&#45;2"></a>3&#46;2&#46;1 Semantics[](#semantics-2)

Elements&#44; attributes&#44; and attribute values in HTML are defined &#40;by this specification&#41; to have certain meanings &#40;semantics&#41;&#46; For example&#44; the <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;ol&#45;element"></a><code>[ol](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-ol-element)</code> element represents an ordered list&#44; and the <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;attr&#45;lang"></a><code>[lang](#attr-lang)</code> attribute represents the language of the content&#46;

These definitions allow HTML processors&#44; such as web browsers or search engines&#44; to present and use documents and applications in a wide variety of contexts that the author might not have considered&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

As a simple example&#44; consider a web page written by an author who only considered desktop computer web browsers&#58;

``` text
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en">
 <head>
  <title>My Page</title>
 </head>
 <body>
  <h1>Welcome to my page</h1>
  <p>I like cars and lorries and have a big Jeep!</p>
  <h2>Where I live</h2>
  <p>I live in a small hut on a mountain!</p>
 </body>
</html>
```

Because HTML conveys <em>meaning</em>&#44; rather than presentation&#44; the same page can also be used by a small browser on a mobile phone&#44; without any change to the page&#46; Instead of headings being in large letters as on the desktop&#44; for example&#44; the browser on the mobile phone might use the same size text for the whole page&#44; but with the headings in bold&#46;

But it goes further than just differences in screen size&#58; the same page could equally be used by a blind user using a browser based around speech synthesis&#44; which instead of displaying the page on a screen&#44; reads the page to the user&#44; e&#46;g&#46; using headphones&#46; Instead of large text for the headings&#44; the speech browser might use a different volume or a slower voice&#46;

That&#39;s not all&#44; either&#46; Since the browsers know which parts of the page are the headings&#44; they can create a document outline that the user can use to quickly navigate around the document&#44; using keys for &#34;jump to next heading&#34; or &#34;jump to previous heading&#34;&#46; Such features are especially common with speech browsers&#44; where users would otherwise find quickly navigating a page quite difficult&#46;

Even beyond browsers&#44; software can make use of this information&#46; Search engines can use the headings to more effectively index a page&#44; or to provide quick links to subsections of the page from their results&#46; Tools can use the headings to create a table of contents &#40;that is in fact how this very specification&#39;s table of contents is generated&#41;&#46;

This example has focused on headings&#44; but the same principle applies to all of the semantics in HTML&#46;

Authors must not use elements&#44; attributes&#44; or attribute values for purposes other than their appropriate intended semantic purpose&#44; as doing so prevents software from correctly processing the page&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; the following snippet&#44; intended to represent the heading of a corporate site&#44; is non&#45;conforming because the second line is not intended to be a heading of a subsection&#44; but merely a subheading or subtitle &#40;a subordinate heading for the same section&#41;&#46;

``` text
<body>
 <h1>ACME Corporation</h1>
 <h2>The leaders in arbitrary fast delivery since 1920</h2>
 ...
```

The <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;hgroup&#45;element"></a><code>[hgroup](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-hgroup-element)</code> element can be used for these kinds of situations&#58;

``` text
<body>
 <hgroup>
  <h1>ACME Corporation</h1>
  <p>The leaders in arbitrary fast delivery since 1920</p>
 </hgroup>
 ...
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The document in this next example is similarly non&#45;conforming&#44; despite being syntactically correct&#44; because the data placed in the cells is clearly not tabular data&#44; and the <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;cite&#45;element"></a><code>[cite](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-cite-element)</code> element mis&#45;used&#58;

``` text
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en-GB">
 <head> <title> Demonstration </title> </head>
 <body>
  <table>
   <tr> <td> My favourite animal is the cat. </td> </tr>
   <tr>
    <td>
     —<a href="https://example.org/~ernest/"><cite>Ernest</cite></a>,
     in an essay from 1992
    </td>
   </tr>
  </table>
 </body>
</html>
```

This would make software that relies on these semantics fail&#58; for example&#44; a speech browser that allowed a blind user to navigate tables in the document would report the quote above as a table&#44; confusing the user&#59; similarly&#44; a tool that extracted titles of works from pages would extract &#34;Ernest&#34; as the title of a work&#44; even though it&#39;s actually a person&#39;s name&#44; not a title&#46;

A corrected version of this document might be&#58;

``` text
<!DOCTYPE HTML>
<html lang="en-GB">
 <head> <title> Demonstration </title> </head>
 <body>
  <blockquote>
   <p> My favourite animal is the cat. </p>
  </blockquote>
  <p>
   —<a href="https://example.org/~ernest/">Ernest</a>,
   in an essay from 1992
  </p>
 </body>
</html>
```

Authors must not use elements&#44; attributes&#44; or attribute values that are not permitted by this specification or <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;other&#45;applicable&#45;specifications"></a>[other applicable specifications](#other-applicable-specifications)&#44; as doing so makes it significantly harder for the language to be extended in the future&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the next example&#44; there is a non&#45;conforming attribute value &#40;&#34;carpet&#34;&#41; and a non&#45;conforming attribute &#40;&#34;texture&#34;&#41;&#44; which is not permitted by this specification&#58;

``` text
<label>Carpet: <input type="carpet" name="c" texture="deep pile"></label>
```

Here would be an alternative and correct way to mark this up&#58;

``` text
<label>Carpet: <input type="text" class="carpet" name="c" data-texture="deep pile"></label>
```

<a id="no&#45;browsing&#45;context"></a>DOM nodes whose <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;node&#45;document"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#39;s <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;bc"></a>[browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-document-bc) is null are exempt from all document conformance requirements other than the [HTML syntax](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#writing) requirements and [XML syntax](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#writing-xhtml-documents) requirements&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In particular&#44; the <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;template&#45;element"></a><code>[template](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-template-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;template&#45;contents"></a>[template contents](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#template-contents)&#39;s <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;node&#45;document&#45;2"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#39;s <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;bc&#45;2"></a>[browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-document-bc) is null&#46; For example&#44; the <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;content&#45;model"></a>[content model](#concept-element-content-model) requirements and attribute value microsyntax requirements do not apply to a <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;template&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[template](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-template-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;template&#45;contents&#45;2"></a>[template contents](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#template-contents)&#46; In this example an <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-img-element)</code> element has attribute values that are placeholders that would be invalid outside a <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;template&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[template](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-template-element)</code> element&#46;

``` text
<template>
 <article>
  <img src="{{src}}" alt="{{alt}}">
  <h1></h1>
 </article>
</template>
```

However&#44; if the above markup were to omit the <code>&#60;&#47;h1&#62;</code> end tag&#44; that would be a violation of the [HTML syntax](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#writing)&#44; and would thus be flagged as an error by conformance checkers&#46;

Through scripting and using other mechanisms&#44; the values of attributes&#44; text&#44; and indeed the entire structure of the document may change dynamically while a user agent is processing it&#46; The semantics of a document at an instant in time are those represented by the state of the document at that instant in time&#44; and the semantics of a document can therefore change over time&#46; User agents must update their presentation of the document as this occurs&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

HTML has a <a id="semantics&#45;2&#58;the&#45;progress&#45;element"></a><code>[progress](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-progress-element)</code> element that describes a progress bar&#46; If its &#34;value&#34; attribute is dynamically updated by a script&#44; the UA would update the rendering to show the progress changing&#46;

#### <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom"></a>3&#46;2&#46;2 Elements in the DOM[](#elements-in-the-dom)

The nodes representing <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;html&#45;elements"></a>[HTML elements](#html-elements) in the DOM must implement&#44; and expose to scripts&#44; the interfaces listed for them in the relevant sections of this specification&#46; This includes <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;html&#45;elements&#45;2"></a>[HTML elements](#html-elements) in <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;xml&#45;documents"></a>[XML documents](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-document)&#44; even when those documents are in another context &#40;e&#46;g&#46; inside an XSLT transform&#41;&#46;

Elements in the DOM <a id="represents"></a><strong>represent</strong> things&#59; that is&#44; they have intrinsic <em>meaning</em>&#44; also known as semantics&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; an <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;the&#45;ol&#45;element"></a><code>[ol](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-ol-element)</code> element represents an ordered list&#46;

Elements can be <a id="referenced"></a><strong>referenced</strong> &#40;referred to&#41; in some way&#44; either explicitly or implicitly&#46; One way that an element in the DOM can be explicitly referenced is by giving an <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;the&#45;id&#45;attribute"></a><code>[id](#the-id-attribute)</code> attribute to the element&#44; and then creating a <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;hyperlink"></a>[hyperlink](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#hyperlink) with that <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;the&#45;id&#45;attribute&#45;2"></a><code>[id](#the-id-attribute)</code> attribute&#39;s value as the <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;navigate&#45;fragid"></a>[fragment](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#navigate-fragid) for the <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;hyperlink&#45;2"></a>[hyperlink](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#hyperlink)&#39;s <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;attr&#45;hyperlink&#45;href"></a><code>[href](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#attr-hyperlink-href)</code> attribute value&#46; Hyperlinks are not necessary for a reference&#44; however&#59; any manner of referring to the element in question will suffice&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Consider the following <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;the&#45;figure&#45;element"></a><code>[figure](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-figure-element)</code> element&#44; which is given an <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;the&#45;id&#45;attribute&#45;3"></a><code>[id](#the-id-attribute)</code> attribute&#58;

``` text
<figure id="module-script-graph">
  <img src="module-script-graph.svg"
       alt="Module A depends on module B, which depends
            on modules C and D.">
  <figcaption>Figure 27: a simple module graph</figcaption>
</figure>
```

A <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;hyperlink&#45;3"></a>[hyperlink](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#hyperlink)&#45;based <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;referenced"></a>[reference](#referenced) could be created using the <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;the&#45;a&#45;element"></a><code>[a](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-a-element)</code> element&#44; like so&#58;

``` text
As we can see in <a href="#module-script-graph">figure 27</a>, ...
```

However&#44; there are many other ways of <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;referenced&#45;2"></a>[referencing](#referenced) the <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;the&#45;figure&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[figure](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-figure-element)</code> element&#44; such as&#58;

- &#34;As depicted in the figure of modules A&#44; B&#44; C&#44; and D&#46;&#46;&#46;&#34;

- &#34;In Figure 27&#46;&#46;&#46;&#34; &#40;without a hyperlink&#41;

- &#34;From the contents of the &#39;simple module graph&#39; figure&#46;&#46;&#46;&#34;

- &#34;In the figure below&#46;&#46;&#46;&#34; &#40;but [this is discouraged](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#figure-note-about-references)&#41;

The basic interface&#44; from which all the <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;html&#45;elements&#45;3"></a>[HTML elements](#html-elements)&#39; interfaces inherit&#44; and which must be used by elements that have no additional requirements&#44; is the <a id="elements&#45;in&#45;the&#45;dom&#58;htmlelement"></a><code>[HTMLElement](#htmlelement)</code> interface&#46;
