If <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;fe&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[value](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#concept-fe-value) is not the empty string&#44; then return &#39;<a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;ltr&#45;5"></a>[ltr](#concept-ltr)&#39;&#46;

    3.  Return null&#46;

2.  If <var>element</var> is a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;slot&#45;element"></a><code>[slot](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-slot-element)</code> element whose <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;root"></a>[root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root) is a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;shadow&#45;root"></a>[shadow root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root) and <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;assigned&#45;nodes"></a>[assigned nodes](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slot-assigned-nodes) are not empty&#58;

    1.  <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;list&#45;iterate"></a>[For each](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate) node <var>child</var> of <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;assigned&#45;nodes&#45;2"></a>[assigned nodes](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#slot-assigned-nodes)&#58;

        1.  Let <var>childDirection</var> be null&#46;

        2.  If <var>child</var> is a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;text"></a><code>[Text](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text)</code> node&#44; then set <var>childDirection</var> to the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;text&#45;node&#45;directionality"></a>[text node directionality](#text-node-directionality) of <var>child</var>&#46;

        3.  Otherwise&#58;

            1.  <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;assert"></a>[Assert](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#assert)&#58; <var>child</var> is an <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;element"></a><code>[Element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element)</code> node&#46;

            2.  Set <var>childDirection</var> to the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;contained&#45;text&#45;auto&#45;directionality"></a>[contained text auto directionality](#contained-text-auto-directionality) of <var>child</var> with <em><a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;auto&#45;directionality&#45;can&#45;exclude&#45;root"></a>[canExcludeRoot](#auto-directionality-can-exclude-root)</em> set to true&#46;

        4.  If <var>childDirection</var> is not null&#44; then return <var>childDirection</var>&#46;

    2.  Return null&#46;

3.  Return the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;contained&#45;text&#45;auto&#45;directionality&#45;2"></a>[contained text auto directionality](#contained-text-auto-directionality) of <var>element</var> with <em><a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;auto&#45;directionality&#45;can&#45;exclude&#45;root&#45;2"></a>[canExcludeRoot](#auto-directionality-can-exclude-root)</em> set to false&#46;

To compute the <a id="contained&#45;text&#45;auto&#45;directionality"></a><strong>contained text auto directionality</strong> of an element <var>element</var> with a boolean <a id="auto&#45;directionality&#45;can&#45;exclude&#45;root"></a><strong><var>canExcludeRoot</var></strong>&#58;

1.  <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;list&#45;iterate&#45;2"></a>[For each](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate) node <var>descendant</var> of <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;descendant"></a>[descendants](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-descendant)&#44; in <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;tree&#45;order"></a>[tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order)&#58;

    1.  If any of

        - <var>descendant</var>
        - any ancestor element of <var>descendant</var> that is a descendant of <var>element</var>
        - if <var>canExcludeRoot</var> is true&#44; <var>element</var>

        is one of

        - a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;bdi&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[bdi](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-bdi-element)</code> element
        - a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element"></a><code>[script](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element)</code> element
        - a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;style&#45;element"></a><code>[style](html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#the-style-element)</code> element
        - a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[textarea](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-textarea-element)</code> element
        - an element whose <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;4"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> attribute is not in the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;undefined&#45;state&#45;2"></a>[Undefined](#attr-dir-undefined-state) state

        then <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;continue"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue)&#46;

    2.  If <var>descendant</var> is a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;slot&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[slot](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-slot-element)</code> element whose <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;root&#45;2"></a>[root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-root) is a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;shadow&#45;root&#45;2"></a>[shadow root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root)&#44; then return the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;directionality&#45;2"></a>[directionality](#the-directionality) of that <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;shadow&#45;root&#45;3"></a>[shadow root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;documentfragment&#45;host"></a>[host](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-documentfragment-host)&#46;

    3.  If <var>descendant</var> is not a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;text&#45;2"></a><code>[Text](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text)</code> node&#44; then <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;continue&#45;2"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue)&#46;

    4.  Let <var>result</var> be the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;text&#45;node&#45;directionality&#45;2"></a>[text node directionality](#text-node-directionality) of <var>descendant</var>&#46;

    5.  If <var>result</var> is not null&#44; then return <var>result</var>&#46;

2.  Return null&#46;

To compute the <a id="text&#45;node&#45;directionality"></a><strong>text node directionality</strong> given a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;text&#45;3"></a><code>[Text](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text)</code> node <var>text</var>&#58;

1.  If <var>text</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;cd&#45;data"></a>[data](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data) does not contain a code point whose bidirectional character type is L&#44; AL&#44; or R&#44; then return null&#46; [&#91;BIDI&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsBIDI)

2.  Let <var>codePoint</var> be the first code point in <var>text</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;cd&#45;data&#45;2"></a>[data](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data) whose bidirectional character type is L&#44; AL&#44; or R&#46;

3.  If <var>codePoint</var> is of bidirectional character type AL or R&#44; then return &#39;<a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;rtl&#45;3"></a>[rtl](#concept-rtl)&#39;&#46;

4.  If <var>codePoint</var> is of bidirectional character type L&#44; then return &#39;<a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;ltr&#45;6"></a>[ltr](#concept-ltr)&#39;&#46;

To compute the <a id="parent&#45;directionality"></a><strong>parent directionality</strong> given an element <var>element</var>&#58;

1.  Let <var>parentNode</var> be <var>element</var>&#39;s parent node&#46;

2.  If <var>parentNode</var> is a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;shadow&#45;root&#45;4"></a>[shadow root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root)&#44; then return the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;directionality&#45;3"></a>[directionality](#the-directionality) of <var>parentNode</var>&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;documentfragment&#45;host&#45;2"></a>[host](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-documentfragment-host)&#46;

3.  If <var>parentNode</var> is an element&#44; then return the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;directionality&#45;4"></a>[directionality](#the-directionality) of <var>parentNode</var>&#46;

4.  Return &#39;<a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;ltr&#45;7"></a>[ltr](#concept-ltr)&#39;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This attribute [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#bidireq)&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <a id="directionality&#45;of&#45;the&#45;attribute"></a><strong>directionality of an attribute</strong> of an <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;html&#45;elements&#45;3"></a>[HTML element](#html-elements)&#44; which is used when the text of that attribute is to be included in the rendering in some manner&#44; is determined as per the first appropriate set of steps from the following list&#58;

<strong>If the attribute is a <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;directionality&#45;capable&#45;attribute"></a>[directionality&#45;capable attribute](#directionality-capable-attribute) and the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;5"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> attribute is in the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;auto&#45;state&#45;3"></a>[Auto](#attr-dir-auto-state) state</strong>

Find the first character &#40;in logical order&#41; of the attribute&#39;s value that is of bidirectional character type L&#44; AL&#44; or R&#46; [&#91;BIDI&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsBIDI)

If such a character is found and it is of bidirectional character type AL or R&#44; the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;directionality&#45;of&#45;the&#45;attribute"></a>[directionality of the attribute](#directionality-of-the-attribute) is &#39;<a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;rtl&#45;4"></a>[rtl](#concept-rtl)&#39;&#46;

Otherwise&#44; the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;directionality&#45;of&#45;the&#45;attribute&#45;2"></a>[directionality of the attribute](#directionality-of-the-attribute) is &#39;<a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;ltr&#45;8"></a>[ltr](#concept-ltr)&#39;&#46;

<strong>Otherwise</strong>

The <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;directionality&#45;of&#45;the&#45;attribute&#45;3"></a>[directionality of the attribute](#directionality-of-the-attribute) is the same as <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;directionality&#45;5"></a>[the element&#39;s directionality](#the-directionality)&#46;

The following attributes are <a id="directionality&#45;capable&#45;attribute"></a><strong>directionality&#45;capable attributes</strong>&#58;

- <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;th&#45;abbr"></a><code>[abbr](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-th-abbr)</code> on <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;th&#45;element"></a><code>[th](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-th-element)</code> elements
- <code>alt</code> on <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;area&#45;alt"></a><code>[area](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#attr-area-alt)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[img](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#attr-img-alt)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;alt"></a><code>[input](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-input-alt)</code> elements
- <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;meta&#45;content"></a><code>[content](html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#attr-meta-content)</code> on <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;meta&#45;element"></a><code>[meta](html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#the-meta-element)</code> elements&#44; if the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;meta&#45;name"></a><code>[name](html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#attr-meta-name)</code> attribute specifies a metadata name whose value is primarily intended to be human&#45;readable rather than machine&#45;readable
- <code>label</code> on <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;optgroup&#45;label"></a><code>[optgroup](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-optgroup-label)</code>&#44; <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;option&#45;label"></a><code>[option](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-option-label)</code>&#44; and <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;track&#45;label"></a><code>[track](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#attr-track-label)</code> elements
- <code>placeholder</code> on <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;placeholder"></a><code>[input](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-input-placeholder)</code> and <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;textarea&#45;placeholder"></a><code>[textarea](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-textarea-placeholder)</code> elements
- <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;title"></a><code>[title](#attr-title)</code> on all <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;html&#45;elements&#45;4"></a>[HTML elements](#html-elements)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<strong><code><var>document</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;dir&#45;dev"></a>[dir](#dom-dir) &#91; &#61; <var>value</var> &#93;</code></strong>

Returns <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;html&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[the <code>html</code> element](#the-html-element-2)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;6"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> attribute&#39;s value&#44; if any&#46;

Can be set&#44; to either &#34;<code>ltr</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>rtl</code>&#34;&#44; or &#34;<code>auto</code>&#34; to replace <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;html&#45;element&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[the <code>html</code> element](#the-html-element-2)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;7"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> attribute&#39;s value&#46;

If there is no <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;html&#45;element&#45;2&#45;3"></a>[<code>html</code> element](#the-html-element-2)&#44; returns the empty string and ignores new values&#46;

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[HTMLElement&#47;dir](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/dir)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox1&#43;Safari3&#43;Chrome1&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera12&#46;1&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer5&#46;5&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS1&#43;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android12&#46;1&#43;

The <a id="dom&#45;dir"></a><strong><code>dir</code></strong> IDL attribute on an element must <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;reflect"></a>[reflect](#reflect) the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;8"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> content attribute of that element&#44; <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;limited&#45;to&#45;only&#45;known&#45;values"></a>[limited to only known values](#limited-to-only-known-values)&#46;

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Document&#47;dir](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/dir)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox1&#43;Safari10&#46;1&#43;Chrome64&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera51&#43;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet Explorer5&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android47&#43;

The <a id="dom&#45;document&#45;dir"></a><strong><code>dir</code></strong> IDL attribute on <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](#document)</code> objects must <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;reflect&#45;2"></a>[reflect](#reflect) the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;9"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> content attribute of <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;html&#45;element&#45;2&#45;4"></a>[the <code>html</code> element](#the-html-element-2)&#44; if any&#44; <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;limited&#45;to&#45;only&#45;known&#45;values&#45;2"></a>[limited to only known values](#limited-to-only-known-values)&#46; If there is no such element&#44; then the attribute must return the empty string and do nothing on setting&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Authors are strongly encouraged to use the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;10"></a><code>[dir](#attr-dir)</code> attribute to indicate text direction rather than using CSS&#44; since that way their documents will continue to render correctly even in the absence of CSS &#40;e&#46;g&#46; as interpreted by search engines&#41;&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This markup fragment is of an IM conversation&#46;

``` text
<p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> How do you write "What's your name?" in Arabic?</p>
<p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> ما اسمك؟</p>
<p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> Thanks.</p>
<p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> That's written "شكرًا".</p>
<p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> Do you know how to write "Please"?</p>
<p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> "من فضلك", right?</p>
```

Given a suitable style sheet and the default alignment styles for the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;p&#45;element"></a><code>[p](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-p-element)</code> element&#44; namely to align the text to the <em>start edge</em> of the paragraph&#44; the resulting rendering could be as follows&#58;

![Each paragraph rendered as a separate block&#44; with the paragraphs left&#45;aligned except the second paragraph and the last one&#44; which would be right aligned&#44; with the usernames &#40;&#39;Student&#39; and &#39;Teacher&#39; in this example&#41; flush right&#44; with a colon to their left&#44; and the text first to the left of that&#46;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/im.png)

As noted earlier&#44; the <a id="the&#45;dir&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;dir&#45;auto"></a><code>[auto](#attr-dir-auto)</code> value is not a panacea&#46; The final paragraph in this example is misinterpreted as being right&#45;to&#45;left text&#44; since it begins with an Arabic character&#44; which causes the &#34;right&#63;&#34; to be to the left of the Arabic text&#46;

##### <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute"></a>3&#46;2&#46;6&#46;5 The <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;style"></a><code>[style](#attr-style)</code> attribute[](#the-style-attribute)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Global&#95;attributes&#47;style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/style)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox1&#43;Safari1&#43;Chrome1&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera&#63;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet ExplorerYes

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android&#63;

All <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;html&#45;elements"></a>[HTML elements](#html-elements) may have the <a id="attr&#45;style"></a><strong><code>style</code></strong> content attribute set&#46; This is a <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;css&#45;styling&#45;attribute"></a>[style attribute](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-style-attr/#style-attribute) as defined by CSS Style Attributes&#46; [&#91;CSSATTR&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSSATTR)

In user agents that support CSS&#44; the attribute&#39;s value must be parsed when the attribute is added or has its value changed&#44; according to the rules given for <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;css&#45;styling&#45;attribute&#45;2"></a>[style attributes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-style-attr/#style-attribute)&#46; [&#91;CSSATTR&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSSATTR)

However&#44; if the <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;should&#45;element&#39;s&#45;inline&#45;behavior&#45;be&#45;blocked&#45;by&#45;content&#45;security&#45;policy"></a>[Should element&#39;s inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy&#63;](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-inline) algorithm returns &#34;<code>Blocked</code>&#34; when executed upon the attribute&#39;s <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;element"></a>[element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element)&#44; &#34;<code>style attribute</code>&#34;&#44; and the attribute&#39;s value&#44; then the style rules defined in the attribute&#39;s value must not be applied to the <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;element&#45;2"></a>[element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-element)&#46; [&#91;CSP&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSP)

Documents that use <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;style&#45;2"></a><code>[style](#attr-style)</code> attributes on any of their elements must still be comprehensible and usable if those attributes were removed&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

In particular&#44; using the <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;style&#45;3"></a><code>[style](#attr-style)</code> attribute to hide and show content&#44; or to convey meaning that is otherwise not included in the document&#44; is non&#45;conforming&#46; &#40;To hide and show content&#44; use the <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;hidden"></a><code>[hidden](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-hidden)</code> attribute&#46;&#41;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;style&#45;dev"></a>[style](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-elementcssinlinestyle-style)</code></strong>

Returns a <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;cssstyledeclaration"></a><code>[CSSStyleDeclaration](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#the-cssstyledeclaration-interface)</code> object for the element&#39;s <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;style&#45;4"></a><code>[style](#attr-style)</code> attribute&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;dom&#45;style"></a><code>[style](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-elementcssinlinestyle-style)</code> IDL attribute is defined in CSS Object Model&#46; [&#91;CSSOM&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSSOM)

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example&#44; the words that refer to colors are marked up using the <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;span&#45;element"></a><code>[span](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-span-element)</code> element and the <a id="the&#45;style&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;style&#45;5"></a><code>[style](#attr-style)</code> attribute to make those words show up in the relevant colors in visual media&#46;

``` text
<p>My sweat suit is <span style="color: green; background:
transparent">green</span> and my eyes are <span style="color: blue;
background: transparent">blue</span>.</p>
```

##### <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes"></a>3&#46;2&#46;6&#46;6 <strong>Embedding custom non&#45;visible data</strong> with the <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;data&#45;&#42;"></a><code>[data&#45;&#42;](#attr-data-*)</code> attributes[](#embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data-*-attributes)

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[Global&#95;attributes&#47;data&#45;&#42;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/data-*)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox6&#43;Safari5&#46;1&#43;Chrome7&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera&#63;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;12&#43;Internet ExplorerYes

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android&#63;

A <a id="custom&#45;data&#45;attribute"></a><strong>custom data attribute</strong> is an attribute in no namespace whose name starts with the string &#34;<a id="attr&#45;data&#45;&#42;"></a><strong><code>data&#45;</code></strong>&#34;&#44; has at least one character after the hyphen&#44; is a <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;valid&#45;attribute&#45;local&#45;name"></a>[valid attribute local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-attribute-local-name)&#44; and contains no <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;uppercase&#45;ascii&#45;letters"></a>[ASCII upper alphas](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-upper-alpha)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

All attribute names on <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;html&#45;elements"></a>[HTML elements](#html-elements) in <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;html&#45;documents"></a>[HTML documents](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document) get ASCII&#45;lowercased automatically&#44; so the restriction on ASCII uppercase letters doesn&#39;t affect such documents&#46;

<a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;custom&#45;data&#45;attribute"></a>[Custom data attributes](#custom-data-attribute) are intended to store custom data&#44; state&#44; annotations&#44; and similar&#44; private to the page or application&#44; for which there are no more appropriate attributes or elements&#46;

These attributes are not intended for use by software that is not known to the administrators of the site that uses the attributes&#46; For generic extensions that are to be used by multiple independent tools&#44; either this specification should be extended to provide the feature explicitly&#44; or a technology like <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;microdata"></a>[microdata](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#microdata) should be used &#40;with a standardized vocabulary&#41;&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For instance&#44; a site about music could annotate list items representing tracks in an album with custom data attributes containing the length of each track&#46; This information could then be used by the site itself to allow the user to sort the list by track length&#44; or to filter the list for tracks of certain lengths&#46;

``` text
<ol>
 <li data-length="2m11s">Beyond The Sea</li>
 ...
</ol>
```

It would be inappropriate&#44; however&#44; for the user to use generic software not associated with that music site to search for tracks of a certain length by looking at this data&#46;

This is because these attributes are intended for use by the site&#39;s own scripts&#44; and are not a generic extension mechanism for publicly&#45;usable metadata&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Similarly&#44; a page author could write markup that provides information for a translation tool that they are intending to use&#58;

``` text
<p>The third <span data-mytrans-de="Anspruch">claim</span> covers the case of <span
translate="no">HTML</span> markup.</p>
```

In this example&#44; the &#34;<code>data&#45;mytrans&#45;de</code>&#34; attribute gives specific text for the MyTrans product to use when translating the phrase &#34;claim&#34; to German&#46; However&#44; the standard <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;translate"></a><code>[translate](#attr-translate)</code> attribute is used to tell it that in all languages&#44; &#34;HTML&#34; is to remain unchanged&#46; When a standard attribute is available&#44; there is no need for a <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;custom&#45;data&#45;attribute&#45;2"></a>[custom data attribute](#custom-data-attribute) to be used&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In this example&#44; custom data attributes are used to store the result of a feature detection for <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;paymentrequest"></a><code>[PaymentRequest](https://w3c.github.io/payment-request/#dom-paymentrequest)</code>&#44; which could be used in CSS to style a checkout page differently&#46;

``` text
<script>
 if ('PaymentRequest' in window) {
   document.documentElement.dataset.hasPaymentRequest = '';
 }
</script>
```

Here&#44; the <code>data&#45;has&#45;payment&#45;request</code> attribute is effectively being used as a <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;boolean&#45;attribute"></a>[boolean attribute](#boolean-attribute)&#59; it is enough to check the presence of the attribute&#46; However&#44; if the author so wishes&#44; it could later be populated with some value&#44; maybe to indicate limited functionality of the feature&#46;

Every <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;html&#45;elements&#45;2"></a>[HTML element](#html-elements) may have any number of <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;custom&#45;data&#45;attribute&#45;3"></a>[custom data attributes](#custom-data-attribute) specified&#44; with any value&#46;

Authors should carefully design such extensions so that when the attributes are ignored and any associated CSS dropped&#44; the page is still usable&#46;

User agents must not derive any implementation behavior from these attributes or values&#46; Specifications intended for user agents must not define these attributes to have any meaningful values&#46;

JavaScript libraries may use the <a id="embedding&#45;custom&#45;non&#45;visible&#45;data&#45;with&#45;the&#45;data&#45;&#42;&#45;attributes&#58;custom&#45;data&#45;attribute&#45;4"></a>[custom data attributes](#custom-data-attribute)&#44; as they are considered to be part of the page on which they are used&#46; Authors of libraries that are reused by many authors are encouraged to include their name in the attribute names&#44; to reduce the risk of clashes&#46; Where it makes sense&#44; library authors are also encouraged to make the exact name used in the attribute names customizable&#44; so that libraries whose authors unknowingly picked the same name can be used on the same page&#44; and so that multiple versions of a particular library can be used on the same page even when those versions are not mutually compatible&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; a library called &#34;DoQuery&#34; could use attribute names like <code>data&#45;doquery&#45;range</code>&#44; and a library called &#34;jJo&#34; could use attributes names like <code>data&#45;jjo&#45;range</code>&#46; The jJo library could also provide an API to set which prefix to use &#40;e&#46;g&#46; <code>J&#46;setDataPrefix&#40;&#39;j2&#39;&#41;</code>&#44; making the attributes have names like <code>data&#45;j2&#45;range</code>&#41;&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<strong><code><var>element</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;dataset&#45;dev"></a>[dataset](#dom-dataset)</code></strong>

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[HTMLElement&#47;dataset](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/dataset)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox6&#43;Safari5&#46;1&#43;Chrome7&#43;

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox51&#43;Safari5&#46;1&#43;Chrome55&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------
